Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly tie-out of policy admin and claims extracts to technical provisions and the Art. 70 reconciliation reserve build; unexplained variances escalate to the Chief Actuary

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 70 (reconciliation reserve) and Art. 260(1)(a) re-read on the consolidated EUR-Lex text at each quarter-end, together with the current EIOPA Annex II instructions for templates S.23.01 (own funds) and S.02.01 (balance sheet)

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly Solvency II close: policy admin and claims extraction → actuarial data validation → best estimate and risk margin → SII balance sheet → own funds classification → reconciliation reserve, for every life, health and non-life solo entity consolidated into the SII group

In-scope systems.value: Reserving models fed from the policy administration system and claims platform through the enterprise data warehouse; own funds assembled in the close/consolidation tool and reported on S.23.01

Compliance procedure documented.value: Quarterly Reserve Data Reconciliation and Reconciliation Reserve Procedure — extract controls and hash totals, policy/claim count and premium tie-outs, best-estimate movement analysis, Art. 70 build-up, sign-off sequence

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the Head of Capital Management; re-approved each year-end and on any policy admin migration, chart-of-accounts change or model change that alters the data feed

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Solo quarterly QRTs (S.02.01, S.12.01/S.17.01, S.23.01) due to the NCA 5 weeks after the quarter-end reference date; solo annual 14 weeks; group quarterly 11 weeks; group annual 20 weeks — the reconciliation must be signed 10 working days before each submission window closes

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close-calendar tasks fire at working day 5 (extract frozen), day 10 (tie-out complete) and day 15 (actuarial sign-off) after each quarter end, with automatic escalation to the Chief Actuary if any tie-out is still open at day 20

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Reconciliation report, extract row counts and hash totals, variance explanations, the Art. 70 build-up and the signed certificate retained 10 years from the reporting reference date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any residual difference above the materiality bar is raised as a Solvency II data-quality issue with root cause, owner and the quarter it must be cleared by; repeat issues are reported to the Risk Committee

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the quarterly reconciliation certificate and personally approves any write-off of a residual unexplained difference

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every reconciling line between the quarter-end policy administration and claims extracts and the technical provisions, excess of assets over liabilities and reconciliation reserve reported on S.02.01 and S.23.01, per solo entity and per homogeneous risk group

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Unexplained difference must be below 0.5% of gross best estimate and below EUR 5m per solo entity; any unexplained movement in the reconciliation reserve above EUR 1m, or any extract row-count gap over 0.1%, is an outright fail

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have run the reserving models, prepared the extract or assembled the own-funds schedule for the quarter under test

checklist.step: Freeze the quarter-end data cut
actions: On the close calendar's day-2 task, run the quarter-end snapshot job in the warehouse orchestrator against the policy, claims and premium source tables with the reference date set to the last calendar day of the quarter.
Record the snapshot id, run timestamp, row count and SHA-256 hash total for each source table in the data-cut register.
Lock the snapshot tables read-only and notify the Reserving Actuary and Data Quality Analyst in the close channel that the cut is frozen.
Where a source system posts late entries after the cut, capture them in a dated post-cut adjustment table rather than re-running the snapshot.
checklist.done: a locked, hashed snapshot exists for every source table with the row counts published to the actuarial team.

checklist.step: Extract the policy and claim inventory from the policy administration system
actions: Run the reserving extract job for each writing entity with valuation date = quarter end, pulling policy number, product code, inception and expiry dates, sum insured, gross written and earned premium, and unearned premium reserve.
Run the companion claims extract for paid to date, outstanding case reserve, claim status and date of loss, keyed on claim number and policy number.
Split the output by Solvency II line of business per Delegated Regulation Annex I and by homogeneous risk group as defined in the reserving methodology paper.
Compare the record counts to the frozen warehouse snapshot supplied by the Data Engineer and investigate any difference before proceeding.
Deposit the extracts in the actuarial data area named <entity>-<YYYYQn>-reserving-extract and log the file hashes.
checklist.done: policy and claim extracts exist per entity, split by SII line of business, with record counts equal to the frozen snapshot.

checklist.step: Validate the extract against the data quality rule set
actions: Run the Solvency II data quality rule pack over the extract: null checks on valuation-critical fields, date sanity (inception ≤ loss date ≤ valuation date), negative reserve checks, currency code validity and duplicate policy/claim keys.
Score each rule against the accuracy, completeness and appropriateness dimensions required by Delegated Regulation Art. 19 and record the pass rate.
Send failed records back to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Claims Director / Manager as a correction list with a 5-working-day turnaround.
Where a failure cannot be corrected in the quarter, document the actuarial adjustment applied and its rationale on the data quality dashboard.
checklist.done: every rule has a recorded pass rate and every failed record is either corrected at source or covered by a documented actuarial adjustment.

checklist.step: Tie the extracted premium and policy counts to the general ledger
actions: Pull the quarter-to-date trial balance for gross written premium, earned premium and unearned premium reserve by entity and line of business from the GL.
Build a three-column tie-out: extract total, GL balance, difference — one row per entity and SII line of business.

Obtain from the Controller the reconciling items that legitimately sit between the systems (suspense premium, broker bordereaux in transit, intercompany eliminations) and post them on the schedule with reference to the GL journal number.
Escalate any unexplained difference above 0.5% of the GL balance to the Reserving Actuary the same day.
checklist.done: the premium tie-out schedule is complete with every reconciling item referenced to a GL journal and no unexplained difference above 0.5%.

checklist.step: Tie case reserves and paid claims to the claims platform
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Run the claims transaction report for the quarter by transaction type (payment, recovery, case reserve movement) at the quarter-end valuation date.
Reconcile opening case reserves + new notifications + reserve movements − payments − closures to closing case reserves for each SII line of business.
Confirm reinsurance recoverables carried in the ceded accounting platform reconcile to the gross claims population on the same claim keys.
List every claim moved after the freeze in the post-cut adjustment table and decide, with the Reserving Actuary, whether it is a subsequent event or an in-period movement.
checklist.done: the claims roll-forward foots for every line of business and post-cut movements are classified and documented.

checklist.step: Load the validated data into the reserving models and check the input reports
actions: Import the validated extracts into the reserving run for the quarter and record the model version, assumption set version and run id.
Open the model input summary report and reconcile the loaded exposure, premium and claim totals back to the extract control totals line by line.
Confirm the model has picked up the current quarter's discount curve — the EIOPA risk-free term structure published for the reference date, including any volatility adjustment applied.
Abort and re-run if any input control total differs from the extract by more than a rounding tolerance; never adjust totals inside the model to force a match.
checklist.done: the model run id is recorded and every model input control total equals the extract control total.

checklist.step: Produce the best estimate and risk margin and analyse the movement
actions: Run the gross and net best estimate for claims provisions and premium provisions per SII line of business, and the risk margin on the cost-of-capital basis at 6%.
Build the analysis of change from prior quarter: expected release, new business, experience variance, assumption changes, discount-rate movement, model changes and data corrections.
Require every bucket above the entity materiality bar to carry a written explanation naming the driver and the person who confirmed it.
Send the movement analysis to the Chief Actuary and Head of Capital Management before the balance sheet is assembled.
checklist.done: the analysis of change explains the full movement in technical provisions with no unexplained residual above the materiality bar.

checklist.step: Reconcile technical provisions into the Solvency II balance sheet
actions: Map each model output cell to the S.02.01 technical provision lines and to the S.12.01 (life) or S.17.01 (non-life) detail templates.

Cross-foot S.12.01/S.17.01 totals to the corresponding S.02.01 lines and to the local GAAP or IFRS reserve balance, showing the valuation-difference bridge (removal of prudence margins, discounting, contract boundaries, expense basis).
Confirm assets are stated at Art. 75 fair value and that deferred acquisition costs and goodwill are eliminated from the SII balance sheet.
Have the Statutory Reporting Manager confirm the same asset values feed the statutory accounts reconciliation.
checklist.done: S.12.01/S.17.01 tie to S.02.01 and a documented bridge exists from the statutory reserves to the SII technical provisions.

checklist.step: Compute the excess of assets over liabilities
actions: Take total assets and total liabilities from the completed S.02.01 and compute excess of assets over liabilities as the starting point required by Delegated Regulation Art. 70.
Reconcile the excess to prior quarter and explain the movement by driver: profit or loss, market value movements, technical provision movement, tax and capital transactions.
Confirm the deferred tax asset and liability positions on the SII basis are those approved by the Tax Manager, with the recoverability memo attached.
Record the figure on the reconciliation reserve worksheet as line 1 with a reference back to the S.02.01 cell.
checklist.done: excess of assets over liabilities is computed from S.02.01, reconciled to prior quarter and posted as line 1 of the worksheet.

checklist.step: Deduct own shares and foreseeable dividends, distributions and charges
actions: Extract the carrying value of own shares held directly and indirectly from the investment ledger and post it as a deduction on the worksheet.
Obtain from the Corporate Secretary the board or shareholder resolutions and the dividend policy, and quantify dividends declared but unpaid plus dividends foreseeable at the reference date.
Include foreseeable distributions and charges — interest on subordinated debt due, expected capital distributions to the parent, and any regulator-directed charge.
Get written confirmation from the Chief Financial Officer that the foreseeable-dividend figure is complete for the reference date and attach it to the worksheet.
checklist.done: own shares and foreseeable dividends, distributions and charges are deducted with board resolutions and a CFO confirmation attached.

checklist.step: Deduct other basic own-fund items and restricted own-fund items
actions: List the other basic own-fund items to be removed under Art. 70: ordinary share capital and the related share premium, initial funds and members' contributions, preference shares and their share premium, subordinated liabilities, surplus funds and the net deferred tax asset recognised as own funds.

Quantify the restricted own-fund items — ring-fenced funds and matching adjustment portfolios — and compute the restriction as the notional SCR of each ring-fenced fund compared with its own funds, per Art. 81.
Cross-check every deduction to the tiering table on S.23.01 so that no item is both deducted here and reported as unrestricted Tier 1.
Compute the reconciliation reserve as line 1 less every deduction and record the arithmetic on the worksheet so it can be re-added by a reviewer.
checklist.done: the reconciliation reserve is computed as excess of assets over liabilities less own shares, foreseeable dividends, other basic own-fund items and restricted own-fund items, with each deduction sourced.

checklist.step: Complete S.23.01 and run the cross-template validations
actions: Enter the reconciliation reserve and the tiered own-fund items into template S.23.01 for the reference date and generate the XBRL instance against the current EIOPA taxonomy.
Run the taxonomy validation rules and clear every blocking error, in particular the S.23.01 to S.02.01 excess-of-assets-over-liabilities consistency check.
Reconcile eligible own funds to cover the SCR and MCR against the tiering limits in Art. 82 and evidence the limit test on the worksheet.
Attach the validation log to the submission pack and record the filing reference once the NCA gateway acknowledges receipt.
checklist.done: S.23.01 passes taxonomy and cross-template validation and the acknowledged filing reference is recorded.

checklist.step: Obtain actuarial function sign-off on the reconciliation
actions: Review the reconciliation report, the data quality dashboard and the analysis of change, and challenge any explanation that rests on 'timing' without a named transaction.
Confirm the technical provisions have been calculated on the methodology, assumptions and data documented in the actuarial function report for the reference date.
Sign the quarterly reconciliation certificate stating that the data used is accurate, complete and appropriate, listing any qualifications.
Escalate any qualification to the Chief Risk Officer and the Audit Committee chair in the same week it is raised.
checklist.done: a dated actuarial sign-off certificate exists for the quarter with any qualifications explicitly stated and escalated.

checklist.step: Log residual differences as data quality issues
actions: Raise one issue per residual reconciling difference with the entity, line of business, amount, the systems involved and the quarter first identified.

Assign a root cause from the standard list (source field not populated, mapping gap, timing of bordereaux, manual journal outside the feed, model input override) and an accountable owner in the source function.
Set a remediation date no later than the next quarter-end close and link the issue to the reconciliation report.
Report issues open for more than two quarters to the Risk Committee with a proposed escalation.
checklist.done: every residual difference has an issue with amount, root cause, owner and a remediation date inside the next quarter.

checklist.step: File the reconciliation evidence under the retention rule
actions: Assemble the quarter pack: frozen extract manifests with hashes, data quality dashboard, GL and claims tie-outs, model run log, analysis of change, Art. 70 worksheet, S.23.01 validation log and the signed certificate.
File it under entity / reporting reference date and apply the 10-year retention label.
Confirm the repository index makes the pack searchable by entity, reference date and QRT template code.
Give the Internal Auditor read access to the quarter folder so testing can start without a further request.
checklist.done: the complete quarter pack is filed, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by entity and reference date.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of reconciling lines for the quarter
actions: Pull the frozen quarter-end snapshot directly from the warehouse using the snapshot id in the data-cut register — not the actuarial team's copy.
Rebuild the population as one row per entity, SII line of business and homogeneous risk group, showing extract totals, model inputs and reported S.02.01 values.
Compare your row count and hash totals to the manifest in the quarter pack and resolve any difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete and record the extraction date and query used.
testing.done: the auditor's independently extracted population reconciles to the recorded snapshot hashes and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population back to the source of record
actions: Agree total gross written premium, earned premium and unearned premium reserve in the population to the quarter-end trial balance by entity.
Agree paid claims and case reserves to the claims platform transaction report for the same period.
Vouch every reconciling item over the entity materiality bar to a GL journal number or a named in-transit bordereau file.
List any item supported only by a narrative as an automatic exception.
testing.done: population totals agree to the GL and claims source of record with every material reconciling item vouched to a document reference.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of reconciling lines above EUR 5m and 100% of lines relating to ring-fenced funds or matching adjustment portfolios.
Take 25 further lines by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum 40 lines overall across at least three entities.
Record the seed value, population size, stratification boundaries and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Add every issue left open from the prior quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all material and ring-fenced lines plus prior-quarter retest rows.

testing.step: Re-perform the data quality assessment on the sampled records
actions: Re-run the accuracy, completeness and appropriateness rules from Delegated Regulation Art. 19 over the sampled records without reference to the reported pass rates.
For each sampled policy, trace the valuation-critical fields back to the policy administration screen and compare field by field.
Where an actuarial adjustment was applied instead of a source correction, test that the adjustment is quantified, documented and approved by the Reserving Actuary.
Record every difference, including a correct number supported by the wrong lineage.
testing.done: each sampled record has an independent data quality result and every difference from the reported pass rate is logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the Art. 70 reconciliation reserve build
actions: Take excess of assets over liabilities straight from the submitted S.02.01 rather than the worksheet and recompute the reconciliation reserve yourself.
Deduct own shares, foreseeable dividends, distributions and charges, other basic own-fund items and restricted own-fund items, sourcing each figure to its own evidence.
Compare your result to the reported S.23.01 reconciliation reserve; any difference above EUR 1m is a fail regardless of direction.
Test that no item is simultaneously deducted here and reported as unrestricted Tier 1 own funds.
testing.done: the independently recomputed reconciliation reserve agrees to S.23.01 within EUR 1m with every deduction separately sourced.

testing.step: Test the ring-fenced fund and matching adjustment restrictions
actions: For each ring-fenced fund, recompute the restriction as the fund's own funds less its notional SCR under Art. 81 and compare to the amount deducted.
Confirm the notional SCR used is the one from the current quarter's calculation kernel, not carried forward from an earlier reference date.
Check the same restriction flows consistently into S.23.01, the SCR templates and the group own-funds consolidation.
Flag any fund where the restriction was assumed to be nil without a supporting notional SCR calculation.
testing.done: every ring-fenced fund and matching adjustment portfolio restriction is recomputed from a current notional SCR and agrees to the reported deduction.

testing.step: Trace sampled lines to identifiers and evidence in the quarter pack
actions: For each sampled line, locate the extract manifest hash, the model run id, the analysis-of-change bucket and the QRT cell reference in the quarter pack.
Confirm the model run id used in the reported figures is the same run id recorded on the sign-off certificate.
Open the S.23.01 validation log and confirm the blocking checks were cleared before submission rather than overridden.
Capture screenshots of each traced identifier into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled line traces to a manifest hash, model run id, movement bucket and QRT cell with screenshots captured.

testing.step: Recompute the reporting deadline maths and prove timeliness
actions: Recompute the submission due date as reference date + 5 weeks for solo quarterly, + 14 weeks for solo annual, + 11 weeks for group quarterly and + 20 weeks for group annual.
Compare the NCA acknowledgement timestamp for each template against the recomputed due date and note any submission inside the last 48 hours as a timeliness risk.
Confirm the reconciliation certificate was signed at least 10 working days before submission as the procedure requires.
Treat any resubmission after the deadline as a reportable breach and record the reason code.
testing.done: every submission is proven on or before its recomputed deadline and any late or last-minute filing is documented with a reason.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording entity, line of business, amount, the control that failed and the SII impact on own funds.
Assign a root cause (mapping gap, source data defect, late journal, model override, unsupported deduction) and an owner in the accountable function, not in actuarial by default.
Set a remediation date inside the next quarterly close and require re-performance evidence at closure.
Escalate any exception that changes reported eligible own funds to the Chief Financial Officer and Chief Risk Officer within one business day.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue with amount, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the aggregate unexplained difference as a percentage of gross best estimate and compare it to the 0.5% and EUR 5m thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — and reference the workpaper evidence behind it.
Have the Valuation Actuary who neither ran the models nor prepared the reconciliation sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any own-funds impact to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the financial reporting repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with a stated conclusion, measured exception rate and a dated Audit Committee reporting entry.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns every response to an NCA valuation, SCR/MCR modelling or ORSA query as holder of the Art. 48 actuarial function; delegates drafting but signs the reply

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 48(1)(g), (h) and (i) (opinion on underwriting policy, on reinsurance arrangements, and contribution to the risk management system including SCR/MCR modelling and the ORSA) checked against the consolidated text, plus Delegated Regulation Art. 272 on actuarial function tasks, at the time each response is drafted

In-scope processes.value: Inbound supervisory correspondence handling: NCA query intake → actuarial triage → evidence assembly from the reserving, capital and ORSA files → drafted response → actuarial function sign-off → submission via the NCA portal and correspondence file closure

In-scope systems.value: Supervisory correspondence register and NCA portal submissions (Bank of England BEEDS, Central Bank of Ireland ONR, BaFin MVP, ACPR ONEGATE), with supporting evidence drawn from the actuarial modelling platform and the model governance repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Supervisory Valuation Inquiry Response Procedure — intake and logging within one business day, materiality triage, evidence pack build, factual-accuracy review, actuarial function opinion, legal clearance and portal submission

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the Head of Compliance; reviewed annually and after every supervisory review process (SRP) cycle or thematic review that changes the NCA's expectations

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven — the deadline is the date stated in the NCA letter (commonly 10 to 20 working days); the internal target is the NCA date minus 5 working days for sign-off, and any extension must be requested in writing before the original date passes

Deadline reminders configured.value: On logging an inquiry the register sets reminders at NCA date minus 10, minus 5 and minus 2 working days to the Appointed Actuary and the Regulatory Reporting Manager, with escalation to the Chief Risk Officer if the draft is not complete at minus 2

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Correspondence file — inbound letter, question log, evidence pack, model run references, draft and final response, sign-offs and portal receipt — retained 10 years from the date of the final reply

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed or extended deadlines, responses later corrected, and any NCA finding arising from the reply are logged as supervisory-engagement issues with root cause and disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off any corrective submission to the NCA and any remediation plan agreed in response to a supervisory finding on valuation or modelling

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All supervisory inquiries touching technical provisions, SCR/MCR calculation, internal model or ORSA received in the period, per the supervisory correspondence register, across every solo entity and the group

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on timeliness — any response filed after the NCA date without a written, pre-agreed extension is a fail; any assertion in a reply not traceable to a dated model run or workpaper is also a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the test runs half-yearly over every inquiry closed in the period, with 100% coverage rather than sampling where fewer than 25 inquiries were received

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, reviewed or signed any response in the population being tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Half-yearly supervisory-response test workpaper (register extract, per-inquiry trace, timeliness recomputation, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository under Supervisory Engagement

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Correspondence file per inquiry with the question log, the cited model run ids and workpaper references, and the signed reply — producible to the NCA or to an on-site inspection team within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager is the single channel to the NCA supervisory team; the Appointed Actuary owns technical content and General Counsel clears anything that concedes a breach or commits to a remediation date

checklist.step: Log the inbound supervisory inquiry on the day it arrives
actions: Open the supervisory correspondence register and create an entry with NCA name, supervisor contact, letter or portal message reference, receipt date and the response date stated in the letter.
Attach the inbound letter or the portal message export and tag the subject area (technical provisions, SCR/MCR, internal model, ORSA, reinsurance, underwriting policy).
Assign the Appointed Actuary as owner for any valuation, modelling or ORSA question and notify them plus the Chief Risk Officer in writing the same day.
Set the internal target date at the NCA date minus 5 working days and let the register arm its reminders.
checklist.done: the inquiry is registered within one business day with owner, NCA deadline, internal target date and the inbound document attached.

checklist.step: Break the letter into individually answerable questions
actions: Read the letter and split it into a numbered question log — one row per distinct question, sub-question and data request.
For each row record the reference date the question relates to, the entity or entities in scope, and the template, model or ORSA chapter it points at.
Mark each row as fact (retrieve and state), calculation (re-run and evidence) or opinion (actuarial function view required).
Where a question is ambiguous, draft a written clarification request to the supervisor rather than answering the question you assume was asked.
checklist.done: a numbered question log exists with reference date, entity, source artefact and answer type on every row.

checklist.step: Confirm scope and any extension with the supervisor in writing
actions: Send any clarification questions to the named supervisor by email or through the NCA portal messaging function, quoting the letter reference.
Where the volume of work makes the stated date unachievable, request an extension in writing before the original date, stating the reason and proposing a specific new date.
File the supervisor's reply against the register entry and update the deadline field only when an extension is confirmed in writing.
Never let a deadline pass on the basis of a verbal understanding.
checklist.done: scope clarifications and any extension are confirmed in writing by the supervisor and reflected on the register entry.

checklist.step: Assemble the technical provisions evidence for the reference date
actions: Retrieve the archived model run for the reference date in question and record its run id, model version and assumption set version.
Export the best estimate and risk margin by SII line of business, the analysis of change, and the discount curve applied including any volatility adjustment.
Pull the data quality dashboard and the reconciliation certificate for that reference date so the data basis can be evidenced, not asserted.
Confirm the exported figures agree to the QRTs actually submitted for that period before anything is quoted to the supervisor.
checklist.done: an archived, identifiable model run supports every technical provision figure to be quoted and agrees to the submitted QRTs.

checklist.step: Assemble the SCR and MCR calculation evidence
actions: Export the SCR calculation for the reference date by risk module and sub-module with the correlation matrices and diversification benefit shown.

Where the standard formula is used, evidence the parameters applied and any undertaking-specific parameters with their approval reference; where an internal model is used, cite the model approval decision and the current model change log.
Recompute the MCR under the linear formula and confirm the corridor test at 25% and 45% of SCR and the absolute floor for the entity's business.
Attach the model validation report covering the reference date and the list of open validation findings.
checklist.done: SCR by module, MCR corridor arithmetic and the current validation report are assembled with model version and approval references.

checklist.step: Assemble the ORSA evidence supporting the actuarial function contribution
actions: Retrieve the ORSA supervisory report for the relevant cycle, the board approval minute and the date the report was submitted to the NCA.

Pull the sections evidencing the actuarial function's contribution: overall solvency needs assessment, stress and scenario results, and the reconciliation between the regulatory SCR and the internal view of capital.
List the assumptions the actuarial function challenged during the ORSA and the resulting changes, with dates and author.
Hand the pack to the Appointed Actuary with a note on anything the NCA has previously questioned in this area.
checklist.done: the ORSA pack, its board approval minute and a dated record of actuarial function challenge are in the evidence file.

checklist.step: Draft the response answer by answer against the question log
actions: Write one response section per numbered question, restating the question verbatim before answering it.
Cite the evidence behind each figure inline: model run id, QRT template and cell, workpaper reference or board minute date.
Answer only what was asked; where an answer reveals a further issue, disclose it in a clearly separated section rather than burying it.
Mark any figure that differs from a previously submitted QRT and explain the difference explicitly, with the restatement route if one is needed.
checklist.done: every numbered question has a drafted answer carrying an inline evidence reference and any difference from prior submissions is called out.

checklist.step: Run a factual accuracy review against the source systems
actions: Take the draft and independently re-derive each quoted number from the cited model run, QRT or workpaper without using the drafter's spreadsheet.
Check units, currency, gross versus net of reinsurance, and whether the figure is solo or group — the most common category of error in supervisory replies.
Confirm every date cited (reference date, board date, submission date) against the underlying record.
Return the draft with tracked comments; unresolved comments block sign-off.
checklist.done: every quoted figure and date in the draft has been independently re-derived and all review comments are cleared.

checklist.step: Obtain legal clearance on admissions and commitments
actions: Review the draft for statements that concede a breach of the Directive or Delegated Regulation, or that commit the undertaking to a remediation date.
Where a breach is genuinely present, confirm the separate notification obligations to the NCA are being met rather than relying on this reply to discharge them.
Rewrite speculative or absolute language and confirm privilege positions on any attached internal advice.
Record the clearance with counsel name and date on the matter file.
checklist.done: counsel has cleared the draft in writing and any conceded breach is routed to its own notification path.

checklist.step: Take the actuarial function opinion and sign the response
actions: For opinion-type questions, state the actuarial function view on the underwriting policy and the adequacy of reinsurance arrangements as required by Art. 48(1)(g) and (h), with the reasoning behind it.
Confirm the response is consistent with the most recent actuarial function report to the administrative, management or supervisory body.
Sign the final response with name, function held and date.
Where the actuarial view differs from management's, state the difference in the reply rather than presenting a single reconciled position.
checklist.done: the response carries a dated actuarial function signature and states any divergence between the actuarial view and management's.

checklist.step: Brief the board or risk committee before submission where the answer is material
actions: Decide against the escalation criteria whether the reply is material — restatement, capital impact, model weakness, or a supervisory concern about governance.
Post the draft reply and a one-page summary to the risk committee pack for the next meeting, or convene an out-of-cycle call if the deadline will not wait.
Record the committee's comments and any instruction to amend in the minute.
Confirm to the Appointed Actuary in writing that the reply may be sent.
checklist.done: material replies carry a minuted committee briefing and a written clearance to submit.

checklist.step: Submit through the NCA portal and capture the receipt
actions: Log in to the NCA's reporting portal for the entity (for example BEEDS, ONR, MVP or ONEGATE) and open the correspondence or ad-hoc submission area quoting the original letter reference.
Upload the signed response and each annex, checking file naming, format and size limits published by the NCA before submitting.
Capture the portal acknowledgement — submission reference and timestamp — and paste it onto the register entry.
Email the named supervisor confirming what was submitted and under which reference.
checklist.done: the response is submitted through the NCA channel with an acknowledgement reference and timestamp recorded on the register.

checklist.step: Track and close out follow-up questions
actions: Keep the register entry open until the supervisor confirms closure or 30 calendar days pass without follow-up.
Log each follow-up question as a child entry with its own deadline rather than reopening the original.
Where the NCA raises a finding or expectation, convert it into a tracked action with an owner and a date agreed with the supervisor.
Report open supervisory actions monthly to the Chief Risk Officer and quarterly to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: the register shows a closure confirmation or a lapsed 30-day window, and every NCA finding is a tracked action with an owner and date.

checklist.step: Feed the lesson back into the valuation and reporting process
actions: Review each closed inquiry for the underlying cause — unclear QRT disclosure, weak documentation, methodology the supervisor does not accept, or genuine calculation error.
Raise a process change where the same question is likely to recur, naming the owner and the reporting cycle by which it lands.
Update the actuarial function report and the technical provisions methodology paper where the exchange changed the position.
Circulate a short lessons note to the reserving, capital and reporting teams.
checklist.done: each closed inquiry has a recorded cause, and any resulting methodology or documentation change is owned and dated.

checklist.step: File the correspondence file under the retention rule
actions: Assemble the file: inbound letter, question log, evidence pack with model run ids, drafts with review comments, legal clearance, signed final response and the portal acknowledgement.
File under NCA / entity / inquiry reference and apply the 10-year retention label running from the final reply date.
Confirm the index makes the file searchable by supervisor, subject area and reference date.
Grant the Internal Auditor read access so the half-yearly test can proceed without a further request.
checklist.done: the complete correspondence file is filed, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by supervisor and subject.

testing.step: Build the population of valuation and modelling inquiries for the period
actions: Extract every register entry with receipt date in the period and subject area technical provisions, SCR/MCR, internal model or ORSA, across all solo entities and the group.
Cross-check the register against the NCA portal message inbox and the Appointed Actuary's mailbox for inquiries that were answered but never logged.
Add follow-up child entries so multi-round exchanges are not counted as one item.
Sign the population as complete, recording the extraction date and the sources reconciled.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the portal inbox and the actuary's mailbox, with unlogged inquiries identified as exceptions on sight.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the source of record
actions: For each population row, open the NCA portal submission history and confirm an inbound message and an outbound response exist with matching references.
Compare the deadline recorded on the register to the date stated in the inbound letter itself, not to the register field.
Vouch every extension to a written supervisor confirmation dated before the original deadline.
List any extension supported only by an internal note as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every register entry reconciles to portal records and each deadline and extension is vouched to the supervisor's own document.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of inquiries that resulted in a restatement, a supervisory finding, or an extension request.
Take a seeded random selection of 15 further inquiries, or the whole remaining population where fewer than 25 inquiries were received.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
Carry forward every open action from the prior period's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all restatements, findings and extensions plus prior-period retest rows.

testing.step: Re-perform the technical answer for sampled questions
actions: Open the archived model run cited in the response and re-derive the quoted best estimate, risk margin or SCR figure yourself before reading the reply's narrative.
Confirm the run id cited is the run that produced the submitted QRTs for that reference date and not a later re-run.
Check gross versus net, solo versus group and currency on each figure quoted.
Record any difference, including a right number supported by the wrong run.
testing.done: each sampled technical answer is independently re-derived from the cited archived run and differences are logged.

testing.step: Trace every assertion to a dated evidence artefact
actions: For each sampled response, list the assertions made and locate the workpaper, board minute, ORSA section or validation report cited for each.
Confirm the cited artefact existed at the date of the reply — check document creation and approval dates, not just its presence today.
Flag any assertion supported only by the drafter's recollection or by an undated spreadsheet.
Capture the artefact reference and its approval date into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled assertion traces to an artefact that demonstrably pre-dates the reply, or is logged as unsupported.

testing.step: Re-perform the MCR corridor and SCR module arithmetic quoted to the supervisor
actions: Recompute the MCR linear result and apply the 25% and 45% of SCR corridor plus the absolute floor for the entity's licence class.
Re-add the SCR modules through the correlation matrices and confirm the diversification benefit quoted reconciles.
Where an internal model figure was quoted, confirm the model version cited is covered by the NCA approval and that no unapproved model change sits between them.
Log any arithmetic or version mismatch as a fail regardless of size.
testing.done: MCR corridor and SCR aggregation quoted in sampled replies are recomputed and agree, on an approved model version.

testing.step: Recompute response timeliness against the letter's own deadline
actions: For each sampled inquiry, compute working days from receipt to submission using the NCA's own business calendar.
Compare the submission timestamp on the portal acknowledgement to the deadline in the inbound letter or the written extension.
Check the internal target of deadline minus 5 working days was met, and record replies signed on the deadline day as a process risk even where compliant.
Treat any response submitted late without a pre-agreed written extension as a fail.
testing.done: timeliness is recomputed from the letter's own deadline for every sampled inquiry and every late reply is identified.

testing.step: Test the sign-off and independence chain
actions: Confirm each sampled response carries a dated Appointed Actuary signature and a factual-accuracy review by someone who did not draft it.
Confirm legal clearance exists for every reply containing an admission or a remediation commitment.
For material replies, confirm the risk committee briefing appears in the minutes before the submission date.
Flag any reply signed by the drafter alone as a segregation failure.
testing.done: every sampled reply shows a drafter, an independent reviewer, legal clearance where required and a dated actuarial signature.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording the inquiry reference, NCA, what failed and the supervisory consequence.
Assign a root cause (inquiry not logged, evidence not archived, deadline mismanaged, figure re-derived from an unarchived run, no legal clearance) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require the fix to be evidenced on the next inquiry of the same type rather than by a policy update alone.
Escalate anything that misled the supervisor to the Chief Risk Officer and General Counsel within one business day.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and a named next-inquiry retest.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time response rate and the proportion of assertions traceable to dated evidence.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references supporting it.
Have an Internal Auditor who drafted, reviewed or signed none of the sampled responses sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and open supervisory actions to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time rate and Audit Committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the board and committee architecture, terms of reference, the reserved-powers schedule and the four-eyes evidence; escalates unresolved gaps to the Board Chair and the Chief Risk Officer

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 40 (ultimate responsibility of the administrative, management or supervisory body, non-delegable) and Art. 246(1)-(2) (group-level system of governance), read with Art. 41 and Delegated Regulation Art. 258, re-checked at each annual governance review and on any national transposition change

In-scope processes.value: Board and committee lifecycle for every SII-regulated entity and the group holding company: constitution and terms of reference, reserved-powers schedule, membership and quorum, meeting cadence and papers, key-function reporting lines, minute-taking and action tracking

In-scope systems.value: Board and committee packs, terms of reference, attendance and minutes held in the board portal; governance structure and key-function map maintained in the GRC platform; constitutional documents in the legal document repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Board and Committee Governance Procedure — committee constitution and terms of reference standard, reserved-powers schedule, quorum and conflicts rules, key-function unfettered-access rule, minute standard and action tracking

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board on the recommendation of the Nomination and Governance Committee; reviewed at least annually and on any change to group structure, licence, or an NCA governance expectation

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous obligation with fixed anchors — annual terms-of-reference review before the first board meeting of the financial year, board effectiveness review annually, System of Governance chapter of the SFCR/RSR at the annual reporting deadline, and NCA notification of governance structure changes within the national notification window (commonly 14 days)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Board portal calendar drives the annual meeting cycle; the governance register raises tasks 60 days before each terms-of-reference expiry, 90 days before a scheduled director term end, and immediately on any committee falling below quorum composition

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Terms of reference, reserved-powers schedule, board and committee minutes with attendance, resolutions and the governance map retained 10 years from the meeting date, and permanently for constitutional documents

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Inquorate meetings, decisions taken outside the reserved-powers schedule, unfilled committee seats and overdue board actions are logged as governance exceptions with disposition and the meeting at which they were cleared

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Confirms closure of every governance exception and reports residual items to the Board Chair before the next board meeting

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every board and committee meeting held in the period across all SII entities and the group, plus every terms of reference, reserved-powers item, committee seat and key-function reporting line in force during the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any inquorate meeting that took a decision, any matter reserved to the board decided elsewhere, any committee operating without current board-approved terms of reference, or any key function without a direct reporting line to the board is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the test runs half-yearly over all meetings held in the half, with a full annual re-performance of the governance map and reserved-powers schedule ahead of the SFCR System of Governance chapter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be outside the company secretariat and must not have drafted any terms of reference or minute in the population

Evidence location for test results.value: Half-yearly governance structure test workpaper (meeting population, quorum recomputation, terms-of-reference currency check, reserved-powers trace, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository under Corporate Governance

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Governance map, committee terms of reference, reserved-powers schedule, key-function reporting lines and 24 months of minutes producible to the NCA within 5 business days of a governance review or on-site inspection request

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary owns governance correspondence with the NCA; General Counsel clears any response concerning board responsibility or delegation, and the Board Chair is briefed before any governance commitment is given

checklist.step: Maintain the current governance map for every regulated entity
actions: List every SII-authorised entity, branch and the group holding company with its licence class, NCA and lead supervisor.

For each entity record the board, its committees (audit, risk, nomination, remuneration, investment, with-profits where applicable) and the reporting line of each of the four key functions — actuarial, risk management, compliance and internal audit.
Show which committees are entity-level and which are group-level shared committees relied on under Art. 246, and state the legal basis for that reliance.
Circulate the map to the Chief Risk Officer and the Head of Compliance for confirmation each time the group structure changes.
checklist.done: a dated governance map exists per entity showing board, committees, key-function reporting lines and any group reliance with its legal basis.

checklist.step: Hold current, board-approved terms of reference for every committee
actions: Open the terms-of-reference library in the board portal and check every committee has a version approved by the board within the last 12 months.

Confirm each set covers purpose, delegated authority and its limits, composition and independence requirements, quorum, meeting frequency, standing agenda, right to take external advice, and reporting back to the board.
Route amended terms of reference to the next board meeting as a resolution item and record the approval minute reference on the document.
Retire superseded versions to the archive so only one live version per committee is visible.
checklist.done: every committee has a single live terms of reference approved by the board within 12 months and referenced to its approval minute.

checklist.step: Keep the reserved-powers schedule aligned to the non-delegable duties
actions: Review the schedule of matters reserved to the board against Art. 40 — ultimate responsibility for compliance with Solvency II cannot be discharged by delegation.

Confirm the schedule expressly reserves approval of the system of governance and its written policies, the ORSA and its results, the SCR/MCR results and any internal model change, the SFCR and RSR, the risk appetite statement and the appointment or removal of key function holders.
Cross-check each committee's delegated authority against the schedule so no reserved matter appears as a committee decision right.
Present the updated schedule to the board annually and record the approving minute.
checklist.done: the reserved-powers schedule covers every non-delegable Art. 40 matter and no committee terms of reference conflicts with it.

checklist.step: Verify board composition, independence and the four-eyes requirement
actions: Confirm at least two persons effectively run the undertaking as required by Art. 42(1), naming them and their appointment dates.

Check the board and each committee against its composition rule: number of independent non-executive directors, chair independence, and the prohibition on the board chair chairing the audit committee.
Confirm no committee has a member whose executive responsibility it oversees, in particular that the audit committee has no executive members.
Record any vacancy that breaches composition and open a nomination action with a target fill date within 90 days.
checklist.done: composition, independence and the two-person management requirement are evidenced for every board and committee, with vacancies tracked.

checklist.step: Set and publish the annual meeting calendar
actions: Build the calendar for the financial year with board and committee dates aligned to the SII reporting cycle — quarterly QRT results, the annual SFCR and RSR approval, the ORSA cycle and the audit plan.
Confirm each committee meets at least the minimum frequency stated in its terms of reference.
Publish the calendar to directors and key function holders through the board portal and diarise paper deadlines at 7 calendar days before each meeting.
Add a contingency slot each quarter for out-of-cycle matters so urgent decisions are not taken by written resolution as a matter of habit.
checklist.done: the published calendar meets each committee's minimum frequency and covers every SII cycle approval point.

checklist.step: Assemble and distribute meeting papers to the standing agenda
actions: Build the agenda from the committee's standing agenda in its terms of reference plus the carried-forward action list.
Collect papers from the paper owners against the 7-day deadline and reject any paper without a stated recommendation, the decision sought and the author's name.
Upload to the board portal with access restricted to members and named attendees, and record the distribution timestamp.
Flag late papers to the committee chair before the meeting rather than tabling them without notice.
checklist.done: papers covering every standing agenda item are distributed at least 7 days before the meeting with the timestamp recorded.

checklist.step: Give key function holders direct and unfettered access to the board
actions: Confirm the actuarial, risk management, compliance and internal audit function holders each have a standing right to attend and to report directly to the board or its relevant committee.
Schedule a private session between the non-executive members and each key function holder at least twice a year without executive management present.
Record in the minute that the session took place and whether any matter was raised.
Escalate to the Board Chair any instance where a key function holder's report was filtered or amended by management before it reached the board.
checklist.done: each key function holder has a standing reporting right and at least two minuted private sessions a year.

checklist.step: Test quorum and conflicts at the start of each meeting
actions: Take attendance in the portal and check the number and category of members present against the quorum in the terms of reference before any business is transacted.
Ask for declarations of interest against the agenda items and record each declaration, the member's name and the item it relates to.
Where a member is conflicted, record their recusal and confirm quorum still holds for that item alone.
Adjourn rather than proceed if quorum fails, and minute the adjournment.
checklist.done: each meeting records attendance against quorum, declared conflicts item by item, and any recusal with a re-tested quorum.

checklist.step: Minute decisions with the reasoning and the challenge
actions: Draft the minute within 5 working days recording, for each item, the papers considered, the substance of the debate and challenge, the decision, dissents, and the delegated authority relied on.
For reserved matters, record the resolution wording verbatim and the vote.
Circulate the draft to the chair for review, then to members with the next pack for approval.
Lock the approved minute in the portal and log the approval date; corrections after that point are made by a further minute, never by silent edit.
checklist.done: an approved, locked minute exists for every meeting recording decisions, challenge, dissent and the authority relied on.

checklist.step: Track actions and delegated decisions to closure
actions: Extract every action from the minute with owner, due date and the meeting that will receive the response.
Chase owners at 14 days before due date and report overdue actions on the next agenda with an ageing profile.
Match each delegated decision taken between meetings to the specific delegated authority that permitted it and to the meeting where it was reported back.
Escalate any action overdue by more than two meeting cycles to the committee chair in writing.
checklist.done: every minuted action has an owner, due date and tracked status, and every between-meeting decision is matched to a delegation and reported back.

checklist.step: Evidence group-level governance where committees are shared
actions: For each subsidiary relying on a group committee under Art. 246, hold a board resolution of the subsidiary recording the reliance, its scope and its limits.
Confirm subsidiary-specific matters are actually considered — check the group committee minute names the subsidiary and its numbers, not just a consolidated view.
Confirm the group system of governance is applied consistently across entities and that local NCA expectations are met where they exceed the group standard.
Report to the group board annually on the effectiveness of the shared arrangement.
checklist.done: each reliance on a group committee is covered by a subsidiary board resolution and evidenced by entity-specific consideration in the group minutes.

checklist.step: Run the annual board and committee effectiveness review
actions: Issue the effectiveness questionnaire to directors and key function holders covering composition, information quality, time on risk and capital, challenge, and committee interfaces.
Interview the chairs and at least two key function holders, and commission an external review on the cycle the local governance code requires.
Present findings and an action plan with named owners and dates to the board.
Track the actions through the governance register and report progress at the half-year.
checklist.done: an annual effectiveness review is completed with a board-approved action plan and tracked owners and dates.

checklist.step: Notify the NCA of governance structure changes
actions: Identify notifiable changes: board or key function holder appointments, resignations and removals, committee structure changes and changes in group governance reliance.
Prepare the NCA's notification form for the entity and submit through its portal within the national notification window, commonly 14 days from the change taking effect.
Record the submission reference and acknowledgement date on the governance register against the individual or committee concerned.
Confirm with the Corporate Secretary that the governance map, board portal membership and the SFCR System of Governance chapter are updated to match.
checklist.done: every notifiable governance change is filed with the NCA inside the notification window with an acknowledgement recorded.

checklist.step: Report governance exceptions to the board
actions: Compile the exception list for the period: inquorate meetings, expired terms of reference, unfilled seats, reserved matters decided elsewhere, overdue actions.
Assign each exception a root cause and an owner and set a closure date tied to a specific future meeting.
Present the list at the next board meeting with a statement on whether the Art. 40 ultimate responsibility remained effective throughout the period.
Record the board's response in the minute and carry unresolved items forward.
checklist.done: the board has received a dated exception report with root causes, owners and closure meetings, minuted with its response.

checklist.step: File governance evidence under the retention rule
actions: File approved minutes, attendance records, terms of reference versions, the reserved-powers schedule, resolutions and the governance map under entity and meeting date.
Apply the 10-year retention label to meeting records and a permanent label to constitutional documents and board resolutions.
Confirm the index makes records searchable by entity, committee, meeting date and resolution reference.
Grant Internal Audit and the external auditor read access to the current and prior two years.
checklist.done: governance records are filed with correct retention labels and are searchable by entity, committee and meeting date.

testing.step: Build the population of meetings and governance instruments
actions: Extract from the board portal every board and committee meeting held in the period across all SII entities and the group, with date, committee, attendees and minute status.
Extract the live terms of reference for every committee with its board approval date and the reserved-powers schedule version in force.
Add every written resolution and between-meeting delegated decision recorded in the period.
Sign the population as complete, noting the extraction date and the entities covered.
testing.done: a signed population lists every meeting, written resolution, terms of reference and reserved-powers version in force during the period.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the statutory and calendar records
actions: Reconcile the meeting count to the published annual calendar and explain every cancelled, added or rescheduled meeting.
Reconcile the committee list to the governance map and to the company registry filings for directors in office.
Confirm every meeting in the calendar has either a minute or a documented cancellation approved by the chair.
List any meeting held without a minute as an automatic exception.
testing.done: meetings reconcile to the calendar and the governance map with every gap explained or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of meetings at which a reserved matter was decided and 100% of written resolutions.
Take a seeded random selection of 15 further meetings spread across entities and committee types, minimum 25 meetings overall.
Take 100% of committees whose terms of reference were last approved more than 12 months before the period end.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all reserved-matter meetings, all written resolutions and all stale terms of reference.

testing.step: Recompute quorum and independence for each sampled meeting
actions: Read the quorum rule from the terms of reference in force on the meeting date, not the current version.
Count attendees by category from the attendance record and recompute whether quorum was met at the time each decision was taken, allowing for recusals.
Check the independence and composition requirements were satisfied on the day, including any prohibition on executive membership.
Treat any decision taken while inquorate as a fail requiring legal assessment of the decision's validity.
testing.done: quorum and composition are recomputed against the rules in force on the day for every sampled meeting.

testing.step: Trace reserved matters to a board decision
actions: Take the reserved-powers schedule and list the decisions taken in the period that fall within it — system of governance policies, ORSA, SCR/MCR results, internal model changes, SFCR and RSR, risk appetite, key function holder appointments.
Trace each to a board minute containing the resolution wording, not to a committee minute or a management approval.
Confirm any board delegation relied on was itself within the schedule and was reported back to the board.
Log any Art. 40 non-delegable matter decided below board level as a fail with a legal assessment of the consequence.
testing.done: every reserved matter decided in the period traces to a board resolution, or is logged as an Art. 40 fail.

testing.step: Test the key-function reporting lines in practice
actions: For each of the four key functions, trace the reports actually delivered to the board or committee in the period against the reporting frequency in the terms of reference.
Confirm at least two private sessions with non-executives are minuted for each function.
Interview each key function holder on whether any report was amended or withheld by management, and record the answer.
Compare the version of a key function report in the board pack to the version in the function's own files for two sampled reports.
testing.done: each key function's reporting frequency, private sessions and report integrity are evidenced or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Test the group reliance arrangements under Art. 246
actions: For each subsidiary relying on a group committee, locate the subsidiary board resolution recording the reliance and its scope.
Read two group committee minutes and confirm the subsidiary's own risks, numbers and decisions were specifically considered rather than consolidated away.
Confirm local NCA governance expectations exceeding the group standard are met and evidenced locally.
Flag any reliance operating without a subsidiary resolution as a fail.
testing.done: every group reliance has a subsidiary resolution and demonstrable entity-specific consideration in group minutes.

testing.step: Recompute notification timeliness for governance changes
actions: List every appointment, resignation, removal and committee structure change effective in the period from the governance register and registry filings.
Recompute the notification due date as the effective date plus the national window applicable to the entity, commonly 14 days.
Compare the NCA acknowledgement timestamp to the recomputed due date and log any late or missing notification.
Confirm the governance map and SFCR System of Governance chapter were updated to match each notified change.
testing.done: every governance change is proven notified inside the applicable window with the map and SFCR chapter updated.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with entity, committee, meeting date, the requirement missed and the governance consequence.
Assign a root cause (terms of reference not refreshed, seat unfilled, secretariat capacity, decision taken under time pressure, delegation misread) and an owner who is a director or function head.
Set a closure date tied to a named future meeting and require the closing minute as evidence.
Escalate any inquorate reserved-matter decision to the Board Chair and General Counsel within one business day.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, a director-level owner, a closure meeting and required minute evidence.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Summarise results by requirement — quorum, terms of reference currency, reserved powers, key function access, group reliance, notifications.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — on whether the board retained ultimate responsibility under Art. 40 throughout the period.
Have an Internal Auditor outside the secretariat, who drafted no terms of reference or minute in the population, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and the Board Chair, and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states a conclusion on Art. 40 effectiveness with a dated Audit Committee reporting entry.

checklist.step: Build the annual governance filing inventory
actions: List every regulated entity and, for each, the governance filings due this year: solo SFCR and RSR, group SFCR, CGAD to the lead state, Form B holding company registration, and any Form D or Form F obligation.
Record for each the legal citation, the receiving regulator, the statutory due date and the submission channel.
Confirm the lead state for each US insurance subsidiary from the NAIC lead-state designation before assuming last year's addressee is still correct.
Publish the inventory to the Corporate Secretary and General Counsel and load every due date into the filing calendar.
checklist.done: an inventory exists naming every governance filing, its citation, regulator, due date and channel, loaded into the calendar.

checklist.step: Issue the content request pack to the contributing functions
actions: Send each key function holder and HR a request naming the exact disclosure elements they own, with the prior-year text and the return date of year end plus 4 weeks.
Ask for changes to be marked against prior year so that 'no change' is an affirmative statement rather than silence.
Request the supporting artefacts alongside the text: terms of reference versions, the governance map, remuneration policy, outsourcing register and fit-and-proper summary statistics.
Track returns on the request register and chase non-returns at the due date, not after.
checklist.done: every contributing function has returned marked-up text and supporting artefacts against the requested elements by the due date.

checklist.step: Draft the System of Governance chapter of the SFCR and RSR
actions: Draft section B against the Delegated Regulation Annex XX structure: B.1 general information on the system of governance, B.2 fit and proper, B.3 risk management including the ORSA, B.4 internal control, B.5 internal audit, B.6 actuarial function, B.7 outsourcing, B.8 any other material information.
Describe the board and committee structure, the allocation of responsibilities, the four key functions and their reporting lines, and any material change during the year with its date.
Include the remuneration policy disclosure covering fixed and variable components, performance criteria and the deferral arrangements for persons who effectively run the undertaking.
Where the RSR requires more depth than the SFCR, draft the additional detail into the RSR version rather than publishing it in the SFCR.
checklist.done: a complete section B draft exists covering B.1 to B.8 for the SFCR with the deeper RSR variant drafted separately.

checklist.step: Obtain the actuarial function contribution statement
actions: Write the disclosure of how the actuarial function discharged Art. 48(1) in the year: coordination of technical provisions, opinion on the overall underwriting policy, opinion on the adequacy of reinsurance arrangements, and contribution to the risk management system including SCR/MCR modelling and the ORSA.
Reference the dates the actuarial function report and each opinion were delivered to the board and the minute that received them.
State any qualification given during the year and how it was addressed rather than omitting it from the narrative.
Sign the contribution statement and hand it to the Corporate Secretary for inclusion.
checklist.done: a signed actuarial function contribution statement covering Art. 48(1)(g), (h) and (i) with board delivery dates is in the draft.

checklist.step: Draft the Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure for US entities
actions: Choose and state the reporting level — ultimate controlling person, intermediate holding company, or insurer — and keep it consistent with prior year or explain the change.

Draft the four required content areas: corporate governance framework and structure, board policies and practices, policies and practices of the most senior management, and processes for critical risk management oversight.

Describe director qualification and election processes, board and committee composition, independence determinations, evaluation processes, succession planning and executive compensation linkage to risk.
Confirm with the Corporate Secretary that every statement matches the governance map and the actual minutes, not the intended design.
checklist.done: a CGAD draft covers all four required content areas at a stated reporting level and matches the governance map.

checklist.step: Prepare the Form B holding company registration statement and exhibits
actions: Update the organisational chart showing every member of the insurance holding company system with ownership percentages, domiciles and NAIC company codes.
Complete the Form B items: ultimate controlling person, capital structure, directors and officers of the ultimate controlling person, and the summary of changes since the last statement.
Schedule all affiliate agreements and transactions in force — management, service, tax-sharing, cost allocation, reinsurance and loans — with amounts for the year.
Attach the required exhibits including the audited consolidated financial statements of the ultimate controlling person and the annual enterprise risk report on Form F where required.
checklist.done: Form B is complete with a current organisational chart, affiliate transaction schedule and all required exhibits attached.

checklist.step: Run the consistency check against the underlying records
actions: Compare every factual assertion in the drafts — committee names, meeting counts, member numbers, key function holders, outsourced functions — to the governance map, board minutes and outsourcing register.
Check the SFCR narrative agrees with the quantitative templates published alongside it and with the prior year's narrative where no change is claimed.
Confirm the CGAD and the SFCR do not describe the same group structure in contradictory terms.
Return every mismatch to the drafter with the source reference rather than editing the source to fit the text.
checklist.done: every factual assertion has been traced to a governance record and all mismatches are resolved in the draft.

checklist.step: Take key function and HR attestations on the content they own
actions: Circulate the final draft sections to the actuarial, risk, compliance and internal audit function holders and to the Chief HR Officer for the remuneration and fit-and-proper content.
Require each to attest in writing that their section is accurate, complete and not misleading as at the reporting date.
Record refusals or qualified attestations and escalate them to the General Counsel before the board pack is issued.
Store the executed attestations against the filing record.
checklist.done: a signed attestation exists from every content owner, with qualifications escalated before board approval.

checklist.step: Route the filings for board approval
actions: Post the SFCR, RSR, CGAD and Form B drafts to the board pack with a summary of changes from prior year and the list of attestations received.
Take a board resolution approving each filing in the wording the reserved-powers schedule requires, including the SFCR approval required before publication.
Record the resolution, the vote and any director comment in the minute, and note the date the board approved each document.
Confirm the approved version is the version that will be filed by comparing document hashes before submission.
checklist.done: each filing carries a dated board resolution and the approved version is hash-matched to the version to be submitted.

checklist.step: Publish the SFCR and submit the RSR to the NCA
actions: Submit the SFCR and its annexed quantitative templates through the NCA portal for the entity within 14 weeks of the financial year end for solo, 20 weeks for group.
Publish the SFCR on the undertaking's website on the same day it is filed and keep it accessible for the required period.
Submit the RSR on the supervisory cycle agreed with the NCA — in full at least every three years and as an update in intervening years.
Capture the portal submission reference, timestamp and the published URL against the filing record.
checklist.done: the SFCR is filed and published and the RSR is submitted, each with a captured submission reference and timestamp.

checklist.step: File the CGAD and Form B with the state insurance departments
actions: File the CGAD with the lead state commissioner by 1 June, using the state's electronic filing channel and the confidentiality treatment the model act provides.
File Form B with the domiciliary commissioner of each insurance subsidiary by the state's annual due date, attaching the organisational chart, affiliate agreements schedule and exhibits.
Where the state requires a filing fee or a signed verification page, complete both before submission rather than filing and supplementing.
Record the confirmation number, filing date and receiving analyst for each submission on the filing record.
checklist.done: CGAD is filed with the lead state by 1 June and Form B with each domiciliary state by its due date, with confirmations recorded.

checklist.step: Handle the event-driven governance filings as they arise
actions: Monitor the trigger list: change of control (Form A), affiliate transactions above the state threshold (Form D, 30 days prior notice), key function holder or director appointment and removal (NCA notification), and material change to the system of governance.
On a trigger, open a filing record the same week with the applicable citation, receiving regulator and computed due date.
Prepare and file within the statutory window, and do not complete an affiliate transaction before the Form D notice period expires without the commissioner's approval.
Report every event-driven filing at the next board meeting.
checklist.done: each trigger event has a dated filing record, a filed submission within the statutory window, and a board report.

checklist.step: Respond to regulator comments and file corrections
actions: Log every comment, deficiency letter or follow-up question from the NCA or state department against the filing record with its response date.
Draft the response with the Corporate Secretary and obtain General Counsel clearance before it is sent.
