Where a filed document was wrong or incomplete, prepare a corrected or supplemental filing, obtain board or delegated approval per the reserved-powers schedule, and file it with an explanatory cover.
Where a published SFCR is corrected, re-publish on the website on the same day and note the correction.
checklist.done: every regulator comment has a cleared, dated response and every correction is filed, approved and, for the SFCR, re-published.

checklist.step: Reconcile filings made to filings due at year end
actions: Take the filing inventory and mark each line filed, filed late, or not filed, with the submission reference.
Investigate every not-filed line and determine whether the obligation genuinely did not apply, with the citation supporting that conclusion.
Raise a compliance exception for every late or missed filing with root cause and remediation.
Report the reconciliation to the board and the Audit Committee with the exception list.
checklist.done: every inventory line is closed as filed, justified as not applicable with a citation, or raised as an exception.

checklist.step: File the governance disclosure evidence under the retention rule
actions: File per entity and reporting year: as-filed SFCR, RSR, CGAD, Form B and exhibits, key function attestations, board approval minutes, submission receipts and any correction correspondence.
Apply the 10-year retention label running from the filing date and mark the CGAD as confidential per the model act's confidentiality provision.
Confirm the index makes filings searchable by entity, regulator, filing type and reporting year.
Grant Internal Audit read access to the current and prior two reporting years.
checklist.done: the full filing pack per entity and year is retained for 10 years, confidentiality-marked where required and searchable by regulator and filing type.

testing.step: Build the population of governance filings due and made
actions: Rebuild the filing inventory independently from the entity list, licence records and the NAIC lead-state designations rather than accepting the compliance inventory.
Add every event-driven filing triggered in the year identified from board minutes, affiliate agreement registers and HR appointment records.
Match filings made — portal receipts and state confirmations — to filings due and highlight both directions of mismatch.
Sign the population as complete, recording sources and extraction date.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt inventory of filings due is matched to filings actually made, with mismatches in both directions listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the inventory to the regulators' own records
actions: Open the NCA portal submission history for each entity and list every governance document received with its timestamp.
Open the state department filing confirmations for CGAD and Form B and confirm the receiving state, filing date and confirmation number.
Confirm the published SFCR is actually accessible on the undertaking's website and that the published version matches the filed version.
List any filing recorded internally but absent from the regulator's record as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every filing reconciles to a regulator-side receipt and the published SFCR matches the filed version.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of SFCR, RSR, CGAD and Form B filings and 100% of Form A and Form D filings made in the year.
Take a seeded random selection of 10 key-function-holder notifications from the event-driven population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
Carry forward every exception from the prior year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: the sample covers all annual filings in full plus a reproducible selection of event-driven notifications and prior-year retests.

testing.step: Test disclosure completeness element by element
actions: Build a matrix of required elements — Delegated Regulation Annex XX sections B.1 to B.8 for the SFCR and the four CGAD content areas — against the as-filed documents.
Mark each element present, partially addressed or absent, quoting the sentence relied on for 'present'.
Confirm the actuarial function disclosure explicitly covers the underwriting policy opinion, the reinsurance adequacy opinion and the contribution to SCR/MCR modelling and the ORSA.
Treat a section heading with no substantive content as absent, not partial.
testing.done: a completeness matrix shows every required element as present with a quoted sentence, or logged as absent.

testing.step: Trace assertions to board minutes and governance records
actions: Select 20 factual assertions across the SFCR and CGAD — committee composition, meeting counts, independence determinations, outsourced key functions, remuneration deferral terms.
Trace each to the underlying record: board minute, terms of reference, outsourcing register or remuneration policy in force at the reporting date.
Flag any assertion that describes intended practice rather than what the records show happened.
Capture the source reference and date for each traced assertion into the workpaper.
testing.done: each of the 20 sampled assertions traces to a dated governance record, or is logged as unsupported.

testing.step: Re-perform the board approval and version control chain
actions: For each annual filing, locate the board resolution approving it and confirm the resolution wording covers the document actually filed.
Compare the hash or version reference of the approved document to the as-filed document and log any difference.
Confirm the approval date precedes the submission date for every filing.
Treat any filing submitted before or without board approval as a fail requiring immediate escalation.
testing.done: every filing has a pre-dated board resolution and the approved version is proven identical to the filed version.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory deadlines and test timeliness
actions: Recompute the SFCR and RSR due dates as financial year end plus 14 weeks for solo and plus 20 weeks for group.
Confirm the CGAD due date of 1 June and each state's Form B annual due date from the current filing instructions rather than from last year's calendar.
Recompute the Form D 30-day prior-notice window and confirm no affiliate transaction completed inside it without commissioner approval.
Compare each recomputed date to the regulator receipt timestamp and log every filing late or filed on the final day.
testing.done: every deadline is recomputed from the current instructions and each filing is proven on time or logged as late.

testing.step: Test the attestation and independence chain
actions: Confirm a signed attestation exists from each content owner and pre-dates the board pack issue date.
Confirm the consistency reviewer was not the drafter of the section reviewed.
Check that any qualified or refused attestation was escalated to the General Counsel and reflected in the filed text.
Flag any section filed with no owner attestation as a control failure.
testing.done: every filed section carries a pre-dated owner attestation and an independent consistency review, with qualifications reflected in the text.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with entity, filing type, regulator, the requirement missed and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause (obligation not on the inventory, content owner late, wrong lead state, approval sequencing, instructions not refreshed) and an owner.
Set a remediation date before the next filing cycle and require the corrected or supplemental filing as the closure evidence.
Escalate any missed statutory filing to the General Counsel and the Audit Committee within one business day and assess whether self-reporting is required.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and a named closure artefact.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate and the disclosure completeness rate from the element matrix.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have an Internal Auditor who neither drafted nor approved any filing in the population sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Audit Committee and the Board Chair and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states a conclusion with on-time and completeness rates and a dated Audit Committee reporting entry.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the fit-and-propriety assessment process for directors, persons who effectively run the undertaking and the four key function holders, jointly with the General Counsel for the propriety evidence and the regulatory notification

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 42 (fit and proper requirements and the obligation to notify the supervisory authority) and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 273 (fit and proper policy and procedures), read with the national competent authority's fit-and-proper guidance for the entity, re-checked at each appointment

In-scope processes.value: Appointment and ongoing oversight of SII controlled roles: candidate identification → competency and propriety assessment → NCA notification or pre-approval → appointment → annual reassessment → change-of-circumstance handling and removal, for every board member, person effectively running the undertaking and holder of the actuarial, risk management, compliance and internal audit functions across all regulated entities

In-scope systems.value: Controlled-role register, assessment records and annual attestations held in the HRIS with the regulatory notification filed through the NCA portal and the evidence pack in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Fit and Proper Policy and Assessment Procedure — role scoping, competency matrix per role, propriety screening set, assessment panel, board approval, NCA notification, annual reassessment and the change-of-circumstance reporting duty

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board on the Nomination Committee's recommendation, and by the Head of Compliance for the regulatory content; reviewed annually and on any NCA fit-and-proper guidance change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Assessment must be completed and documented before appointment takes effect; NCA notification of appointment or removal within the national window (commonly 14 days from the change, and prior approval before the person starts in pre-approval regimes such as the UK SM&CR Form A); annual reassessment within 12 months of the last assessment; change of circumstance reported to the NCA within 10 working days of the firm learning of it

Deadline reminders configured.value: The HRIS controlled-role register raises tasks 90 days before each annual reassessment anniversary, immediately on any leaver or role change affecting a controlled role, and daily until an outstanding NCA notification is filed

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Assessment record, CV, qualification and regulatory-reference evidence, screening results, panel notes, board approval, NCA notification and acknowledgement retained 10 years from the date the individual leaves the controlled role

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Appointments made before assessment completion, missed reassessments, late or absent NCA notifications and unreported changes of circumstance are logged as fit-and-proper exceptions with disposition and board reporting

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Approves every retrospective assessment, late notification and any decision to allow an individual to remain in role while a propriety concern is investigated

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every individual holding a controlled role during the period — board members, persons effectively running the undertaking and the four key function holders across all regulated entities — plus every appointment, role change and departure in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any individual appointed without a completed and approved assessment dated before the effective date, any reassessment more than 12 months overdue, or any missing or late NCA notification is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per appointment with continuous ongoing assessment; the test runs half-yearly covering 100% of appointments and departures in the half and a sample of standing role holders' annual reassessments

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be outside HR and Legal and must not have sat on any assessment panel in the population

Evidence location for test results.value: Half-yearly fit-and-proper test workpaper (controlled-role population, per-appointment trace, screening re-performance, notification timing recomputation, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository under People and Governance

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Controlled-role register with assessment dates, the assessment file for any named individual, and the notification history, producible to the NCA within 5 business days of a fit-and-proper or governance review request

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance responds to NCA fit-and-proper queries with the assessment file; General Counsel clears any response concerning an adverse finding, and the Nomination Committee chair is briefed before any commitment on an individual is given

checklist.step: Define and maintain the controlled-role register
actions: List for each regulated entity every role in scope of Art. 42: board members, the persons who effectively run the undertaking, and the holders and deputies of the actuarial, risk management, compliance and internal audit functions.
Record for each role the entity, the regulatory regime and whether the NCA requires prior approval or post-event notification.
Add outsourced key functions with the named individual at the provider who performs the role and the internal person responsible for overseeing them.
Reconcile the register to the HRIS position data and to the governance map every quarter and correct differences at source.
checklist.done: the register lists every Art. 42 role per entity with regime, approval type and named holder, reconciled quarterly to the HRIS.

checklist.step: Set the competency requirements for each controlled role
actions: Build a competency matrix per role covering insurance and financial markets knowledge, business strategy and model, system of governance, financial and actuarial analysis, and the regulatory framework.

State the minimum professional qualification for each key function — for the actuarial function, membership of a recognised actuarial body and the relevant practising certificate where the jurisdiction requires it.
For collective board suitability, record the mix of skills the board must hold and where each is currently held.
Have the Nomination Committee approve the matrix and refresh it annually alongside the board skills gap analysis.
checklist.done: an approved competency matrix exists per controlled role with a stated minimum qualification and a board-level collective suitability view.

checklist.step: Collect the candidate's evidence pack before any offer is made
actions: Request from the candidate a full CV with no unexplained gaps, evidence of professional qualifications and continuing professional development records, and a completed fit-and-proper questionnaire.

Take the questionnaire declarations: criminal convictions, regulatory investigations or sanctions, director disqualifications, bankruptcy and insolvency events, dismissals for misconduct, and civil judgments.
Collect regulatory references from every employer in the last 6 years where the jurisdiction requires them, using the prescribed reference template.
Refuse to progress a candidate whose questionnaire or references are incomplete rather than conditioning the appointment on later receipt.
checklist.done: a complete evidence pack — CV, qualifications, questionnaire and six-year regulatory references — is on file before an offer is made.

checklist.step: Run the propriety screening
actions: Run the standard screening set against the candidate: criminal record check where lawful, credit and bankruptcy search, director disqualification and company officer search, sanctions and PEP screening, and adverse media.
Check the individual against the relevant regulatory registers and public enforcement notices in every jurisdiction they have worked in.
Compare every hit to the candidate's own declarations and treat a genuine hit that was not declared as a propriety concern in itself.
Record the search date, provider, search parameters and result for each check on the assessment record.
checklist.done: every screening check is completed and dated, with each hit reconciled to the candidate's declaration and any non-disclosure flagged.

checklist.step: Hold the assessment panel and reach a documented conclusion
actions: Convene a panel of at least the Nomination Committee chair, the Chief HR Officer and the Head of Compliance, with the incumbent function holder for key function appointments.
Score the candidate against the competency matrix, citing the evidence for each competency rather than an overall impression.
Assess propriety against the screening results and declarations, and where an adverse item exists, record the nature, age, relevance and remediation before concluding.
Write the conclusion — fit and proper, fit and proper subject to conditions, or not fit and proper — with the reasoning and the panel members' names and date.
checklist.done: a dated panel record exists with competency scoring against evidence, a propriety analysis, and a reasoned conclusion.

checklist.step: Obtain board or Nomination Committee approval of the appointment
actions: Put the assessment conclusion and the evidence summary to the board or Nomination Committee as required by the reserved-powers schedule.
Record in the minute the approval, any conditions attached (for example a development plan or a supervised period), and the effective date of appointment.
Confirm the appointment does not breach board composition, independence or the two-person management requirement of Art. 42(1).
Hold the appointment letter unissued until the approval minute exists and any pre-approval notification is cleared.
checklist.done: a minuted board or committee approval exists with the effective date and any conditions, before the appointment letter is issued.

checklist.step: Notify or seek pre-approval from the NCA
actions: Determine from the entity's regime whether the appointment needs prior approval or post-event notification and compute the deadline accordingly.

Complete the NCA's form — for example an individual questionnaire in an EU pre-approval regime or a Form A submitted through the regulator's connect portal — with the assessment conclusion and the disclosed adverse items.
Submit through the NCA portal, attach the assessment summary and references where required, and record the submission reference and date.
Do not allow the individual to begin performing the role until approval is received in a pre-approval regime, and track the statutory determination period.
checklist.done: the notification or approval application is filed within the applicable window with a recorded reference, and no pre-approval role starts before approval.

checklist.step: Complete the induction and record the appointment
actions: Assign the controlled-role induction curriculum: system of governance, the individual's regulatory responsibilities, conflicts and conduct rules, and entity-specific risk and capital training.
Record the induction completion date and any conditions from the panel as tracked development actions with review dates.
Update the HRIS controlled-role register with the individual, entity, role, effective date, assessment date and next reassessment due date.
Confirm the governance map, board portal membership and NCA register entry all show the same effective date.
checklist.done: induction is completed and recorded, and the register, governance map and portal all show a consistent effective date.

checklist.step: Run the annual reassessment of every standing role holder
actions: Issue the annual fit-and-proper attestation to every controlled-role holder 90 days before their anniversary, requiring re-declaration of the questionnaire items.
Re-run the propriety screening set and compare the results to the prior year's file.
Collect evidence of continuing professional development against the hours required by the individual's professional body and the competency matrix.
Record the reassessment conclusion and the date, and escalate any newly disclosed or discovered adverse item to the Head of Compliance the same day.
checklist.done: every controlled-role holder has a dated reassessment within 12 months covering re-declaration, re-screening and CPD evidence.

checklist.step: Handle changes of circumstance as they arise
actions: Operate a standing duty on controlled-role holders to report within 5 working days any charge, investigation, disqualification, insolvency event or disciplinary finding affecting them.
On notification, open a case, restrict the individual's decision-making authority where the concern is material, and record the restriction and who approved it.
Assess whether the individual remains fit and proper, taking legal advice where the matter is contested, and document the reasoning.
Report the change to the NCA within 10 working days of the firm learning of it, whatever the internal conclusion.
checklist.done: each reported change has a case, an interim decision on authority, a documented assessment and an NCA report within 10 working days.

checklist.step: Manage the removal of an individual from a controlled role
actions: Where the conclusion is that the individual is no longer fit and proper, prepare the removal decision with the reasoning and the board approval required by the reserved-powers schedule.
Confirm the key function does not go unfilled — appoint an interim holder assessed to the same standard before the departure takes effect.
Notify the NCA of the removal and the reason within the national window and answer any follow-up question through the Head of Compliance.
Complete any regulatory reference obligations to future employers accurately and within the prescribed period.
checklist.done: each removal has a board-approved reasoned decision, an assessed interim holder, an NCA notification and a completed regulatory reference.

checklist.step: Assess collective board suitability annually
actions: Map the current board's skills against the collective suitability requirements and identify gaps in insurance, actuarial, capital, IT and sustainability risk expertise.
Compare the map to forthcoming retirements and term expiries over the next 24 months.
Present the gap analysis and a succession plan to the Nomination Committee with named development or recruitment actions.
Record the committee's conclusion on collective suitability in the minute for use in the SFCR System of Governance chapter.
checklist.done: an annual collective suitability assessment with a gap analysis and succession plan is minuted by the Nomination Committee.

checklist.step: Oversee fitness and propriety of outsourced key function holders
actions: For every outsourced key function, identify the named individual at the provider who performs it and obtain their CV, qualifications and propriety declarations.
Apply the same competency matrix and screening standard as for internal holders, using the contractual audit and information rights to obtain the evidence.
Confirm the internal person designated to oversee the outsourced function is themselves assessed and registered as the responsible holder.
Require the provider to notify any change in the named individual before it takes effect and treat an unnotified change as a contractual breach.
checklist.done: each outsourced key function has an assessed named individual, an assessed internal overseer and a contractual change-notification duty.

checklist.step: Report fit-and-proper status to the board
actions: Produce a half-yearly report showing controlled roles filled and vacant, assessments completed, reassessments overdue, notifications filed and late, and open propriety cases.
Show the ageing of every overdue reassessment and name the owner for each.
Give an explicit statement on whether all persons running the undertaking and holding key functions were fit and proper throughout the period.
Record the board's response and any instruction in the minute.
checklist.done: the board has received a half-yearly report with an explicit compliance statement, overdue ageing and a minuted response.

checklist.step: Retain the assessment evidence for the full retention period
actions: File per individual and role: CV, qualifications, questionnaire, references, screening results with dates, panel record, board approval minute, NCA notification and acknowledgement, and each annual reassessment.
Apply the 10-year-from-departure retention label and the personal-data handling controls the privacy policy requires for screening results.
Restrict access to HR, Compliance, Legal and Internal Audit and log every access to a screening file.
Confirm the record is retrievable by individual, entity, role and assessment date.
checklist.done: each individual's assessment file is complete, access-restricted, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by role and assessment date.

testing.step: Build the population of controlled-role holders and role events
actions: Extract every individual who held a controlled role at any point in the period, with entity, role, start date and end date.
Add every appointment, internal move and departure in the period from HRIS position history and board minutes.
Include outsourced key function holders and the named individuals at the providers.
Sign the population as complete, recording the extraction date and the sources used.
testing.done: a signed population covers every controlled-role holder and every role event in the period, including outsourced holders.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the regulator's register and the board minutes
actions: Compare the population to the NCA's public or portal register of approved persons for each entity.
Compare it to the board minutes recording appointments and removals and to the company registry filings for directors.
List individuals shown on the regulator's register but not in the population, and vice versa, as automatic exceptions.
Confirm no key function was vacant for more than the period the policy permits, using the start and end dates.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the regulator's register, board minutes and registry filings, with both-direction differences logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of appointments, removals and role changes in the period and 100% of key function holders.
Take a seeded random selection of 15 standing role holders for reassessment testing, minimum 30 individuals overall.
Take 100% of individuals with any disclosed adverse item or open propriety case.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all role events, all key function holders and every individual with an adverse item.

testing.step: Re-perform the fitness assessment against the competency matrix
actions: Take the competency matrix in force at the assessment date and score the sampled individual yourself from the CV, qualifications and CPD evidence before reading the panel conclusion.
Confirm the required professional qualification and any practising certificate were held and in date at the effective date, checking the professional body's register directly.
Compare your scoring to the panel's and treat an unevidenced competency scored as met as an exception.
Capture the register check and evidence references into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled individual has an independent competency re-score with qualifications verified at the professional body's register.

testing.step: Re-perform the propriety screening on the sample
actions: Re-run the sanctions, PEP, adverse media, disqualification and insolvency searches for each sampled individual and compare to the results on file.
Check the original searches were run before the effective date and covered every jurisdiction the individual has worked in.
Reconcile every hit to the individual's declaration and to the panel's documented analysis of relevance.
Treat an undeclared hit that the panel never considered as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: screening is independently re-run for each sampled individual with every hit reconciled to a declaration and a panel analysis.

testing.step: Trace each appointment to approval and notification evidence
actions: For each sampled appointment, locate the panel record, the board or committee approval minute and the NCA notification or approval.
Confirm the assessment conclusion and the board approval both pre-date the effective date on the appointment letter and in the HRIS.
For pre-approval regimes, confirm the regulator's approval pre-dates the first day the individual performed the role.
Capture the minute reference, submission reference and effective dates into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled appointment traces to a pre-dated assessment, board approval and regulatory notification or approval.

testing.step: Recompute notification and reassessment timing
actions: Recompute each notification due date as the effective date plus the national window, commonly 14 days, and compare it to the NCA acknowledgement timestamp.
Recompute each change-of-circumstance report as the date the firm learned of it plus 10 working days and compare to the report date.
Recompute each reassessment due date as the prior assessment date plus 12 months and measure the days overdue for any that slipped.
Log every late item with the number of days late rather than a binary pass or fail.
testing.done: every notification, change report and reassessment has a recomputed due date and a measured days-late figure where applicable.

testing.step: Test the outsourced key function holders to the same standard
actions: For each outsourced key function in the sample, obtain the provider's named individual and confirm an assessment file exists to the internal standard.
Confirm the internal overseer is registered as a controlled-role holder and has their own assessment.
Check whether the provider changed the named individual in the period and whether notice was given before the change.
Flag any outsourced key function relying on the provider's own assurance without firm-held evidence.
testing.done: every sampled outsourced key function has a firm-held assessment file, an assessed internal overseer and evidenced change notice.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the individual, entity, role, the requirement missed and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause (role not on the register, screening run late, references not obtained, notification window misread, reassessment not triggered) and an owner in HR, Compliance or Legal.
Set a remediation date and require the completed retrospective assessment or filed notification as the closure artefact.
Escalate any individual performing a pre-approval role without approval to the General Counsel and Chief Risk Officer within one business day.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue with named individual, root cause, owner, remediation date and closure artefact.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the proportion of appointments assessed before effective date, the reassessment currency rate and the on-time notification rate.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — on whether all persons running the undertaking and holding key functions were fit and proper throughout the period.
Have an Internal Auditor outside HR and Legal who sat on no assessment panel sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Nomination Committee and the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states a conclusion with measured assessment, reassessment and notification rates and a dated committee reporting entry.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Runs the annual written-policy review cycle on behalf of the board — schedule, challenge, approval routing and the post-approval implementation check; escalates overdue policies to the Board Chair

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 41(1) and 41(3) (written policies on risk management, internal control, internal audit and, where relevant, outsourcing; reviewed at least annually and after any significant change) with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 258(1)(c) and 258(2), re-read before the annual review cycle opens

In-scope processes.value: Annual governance policy cycle for every regulated entity: policy inventory and owner assignment → owner review against regulatory and business change → risk, compliance and legal challenge → board approval → publication and staff communication → implementation and effectiveness check, plus out-of-cycle review on significant change

In-scope systems.value: Policy inventory, review workflow, version history and attestation tracking in the GRC platform, with board approval taken through the board portal and the published policy library on the intranet

Compliance procedure documented.value: Written Policy Review and Approval Procedure — mandatory policy list, owner and approver map, annual review calendar, minimum content standard, challenge steps, board approval routing, publication and the significant-change trigger list

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board and reviewed annually as part of the same cycle it governs; changes to the mandatory policy list require Board approval on the Risk Committee's recommendation

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Each written policy must be reviewed and board-approved at least every 12 months from its last approval date and within 3 months of any significant change to the system or area concerned; the cycle is timed so that all approvals close before the SFCR System of Governance chapter is drafted at year end plus 8 weeks

Deadline reminders configured.value: The GRC policy inventory raises tasks at 120 days (owner review opens), 60 days (challenge complete) and 30 days (board pack deadline) before each policy's approval anniversary, with automatic escalation to the Board Chair at 15 days and a breach record at anniversary plus 1 day

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each approved policy version, the review record showing what changed and why, challenge comments, the board approval minute and the communication and attestation records retained 10 years from supersession

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Policies past their 12-month anniversary, approvals taken below board level, policies with no named owner and unactioned significant-change triggers are logged as governance exceptions with owner and closure meeting

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Confirms closure of every overdue-policy exception and reports to the board whether the system of governance operated on approved policies throughout the gap period

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every written policy on the mandatory Art. 41(3) list plus all other system-of-governance policies in force during the period, across all regulated entities, together with every significant-change event logged in the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any mandatory policy without a board approval inside 12 months, any policy approved by management rather than the board, any missing mandatory policy, and any significant change not followed by review within 3 months, is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with event-driven triggers; the test runs annually after the cycle closes, over 100% of mandatory policies, plus a half-yearly interim check on significant-change triggers

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own, draft or approve any policy in the population and must not sit in the secretariat that ran the cycle

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual policy governance test workpaper (policy inventory, approval-date recomputation, content standard matrix, significant-change trace, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository under Corporate Governance

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Policy inventory with approval dates and minute references, the approved version of any named policy, and the significant-change log, producible to the NCA within 5 business days of a system-of-governance review

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance answers NCA questions on the policy framework with the inventory and minutes; the Chief Risk Officer owns any commitment on policy content and General Counsel clears any admission that the undertaking operated without an approved policy

checklist.step: Maintain the mandatory written-policy inventory
actions: List the policies Art. 41(3) and Delegated Regulation Art. 258(1)(c) require: risk management, internal control, internal audit and outsourcing, plus the sub-policies the Delegated Regulation names — underwriting and reserving, asset-liability management, investment risk, liquidity and concentration risk, operational risk management, reinsurance and other risk-mitigation techniques, capital management, fit and proper, remuneration, data quality, and continuity.
Record per policy the entity or entities it applies to, the accountable owner, the approving body, the last approval date and the next due date.
Reconcile the inventory against the published policy library and flag any policy in force that is not on the inventory and any inventory line with no published document.
Have the Risk Committee approve additions and deletions to the mandatory list rather than allowing the inventory to drift.
checklist.done: the inventory covers every mandatory policy with owner, entity scope, approver, last approval and next due date, reconciled to the published library.

checklist.step: Publish the annual review calendar
actions: Schedule each policy's board approval slot so it falls before its 12-month anniversary and spread the load across the year's board and committee meetings.
Align risk and capital policies with the ORSA cycle and the SFCR drafting window so the approved versions are the ones described in the report.
Publish the calendar to policy owners with the 120/60/30-day milestones and load them into the GRC workflow.
Reserve capacity at each meeting for out-of-cycle reviews triggered by significant change.
checklist.done: every policy has a board slot dated before its anniversary and owners have the milestone dates in the GRC workflow.

checklist.step: Open the owner review with a change brief
actions: At the 120-day milestone, send each owner the current approved version, the review record from last year and a brief listing what has changed since — regulatory amendments, NCA guidance, business changes, incidents, audit and validation findings.
Require the owner to respond with a marked-up draft or an affirmative 'no change required' statement with reasons — silence is not an outcome.
Ask the owner to confirm the policy's stated scope still matches the entities and activities it is applied to.
Track responses on the workflow and chase at the milestone date.
checklist.done: each policy owner has returned a marked-up draft or a reasoned no-change statement against a dated change brief.

checklist.step: Check each policy against the minimum content standard
actions: Test each draft against the content standard: purpose and regulatory basis with citations, scope by entity and activity, roles and responsibilities including the key function involved, the risk appetite or limits it operates within, required controls, reporting and escalation, breach handling, review frequency and approver.
Confirm the policy states the specific outcomes Delegated Regulation Art. 258 requires for that area rather than restating the regulation.
Reject drafts that describe aspiration without naming who does what, when and on what evidence.
Record the standard check result against the policy record.
checklist.done: every draft has a recorded content-standard result and no draft goes forward without named responsibilities, controls and escalation.

checklist.step: Run the risk, compliance and legal challenge
actions: Risk management reviews each draft against the risk appetite statement and the ORSA conclusions and challenges any limit that no longer reflects the risk profile.
Compliance checks the regulatory citations are current and that national transposition requirements exceeding the Directive are reflected.
Legal reviews for contractual and employment law consequences, particularly for the remuneration and outsourcing policies.
Record every challenge comment and its resolution on the policy record; unresolved comments block the board pack.
checklist.done: each draft carries recorded risk, compliance and legal challenge with every comment resolved before the board pack.

checklist.step: Verify the policy is actually being operated before re-approving it
actions: For each policy up for approval, pull the operating evidence its own controls require — reports produced, limits monitored, approvals taken, breaches escalated — for the last 12 months.
Report to the board where a policy requirement has not been operated, rather than allowing re-approval of an unimplemented policy.
Bring forward open audit and validation findings relevant to the policy area so the board sees them alongside the draft.
Record the implementation status against each policy record.
checklist.done: every policy going to the board carries an implementation status backed by operating evidence and open findings.

checklist.step: Assemble the board pack with a defensible change summary
actions: For each policy prepare a cover note stating the material changes, the reason for each, the challenge comments received, the implementation status and the decision sought.
Attach a redline against the currently approved version so the board sees exactly what it is changing.
Distribute at least 7 days before the meeting through the board portal and record the distribution timestamp.
Flag to the chair any policy arriving without a redline or an implementation status.
checklist.done: each policy reaches the board with a redline, a change rationale, challenge history and implementation status, distributed 7 days ahead.

checklist.step: Take the board approval resolution
actions: Take a resolution approving each policy by name and version, with the effective date, recorded in the minute in the wording the reserved-powers schedule requires.
Record the board's challenge, any conditions attached and any dissent.
Where the board defers a policy, record the deferral, the reason and the date it must return — and note that the existing approved version remains in force meanwhile.
Confirm approval was taken by the board itself for the four Art. 41(3) policies rather than by a committee under delegation.
checklist.done: a minuted board resolution names each approved policy, its version and effective date, with deferrals and dissent recorded.

checklist.step: Publish the approved version and retire the superseded one
actions: Publish the approved version to the policy library with version number, approval date, minute reference, effective date and next review date on the cover page.
Move the superseded version to the archive so exactly one live version per policy is visible to staff.
Update the GRC policy record with the new approval and next-due dates so the reminder clock restarts from the correct anchor.
Confirm the published version is byte-identical to the version the board approved.
checklist.done: one live, board-stamped version is published per policy, the superseded version is archived and the GRC due dates are reset.

checklist.step: Communicate changes and take attestations where behaviour changes
actions: Identify the populations affected by each material change and write a plain-language summary of what they must now do differently.
Assign attestation or training in the learning management system where the change alters an individual's obligations, with a completion deadline of 30 days.
Track completion and escalate non-completers to their function head at the deadline.
Record the communication date, population size and completion rate on the policy record.
checklist.done: each material change has a targeted communication and, where behaviour changes, tracked attestation with a measured completion rate.

checklist.step: Operate the significant-change trigger outside the annual cycle
actions: Maintain the trigger list: regulatory amendment, material acquisition or disposal, new line of business or territory, internal model change, major outsourcing arrangement, material incident or breach, and adverse ORSA or validation finding.
On a trigger, open an out-of-cycle review record naming the affected policies and set the review deadline at 3 months from the change.
Route the resulting amendments to the next board or committee meeting rather than waiting for the annual slot.
Report open triggers and their ageing to the Risk Committee each quarter.
checklist.done: every logged significant change has a named affected-policy list and a board-routed review inside 3 months.

checklist.step: Cascade group policies to subsidiaries and record local adoption
actions: Distribute each board-approved group policy to every subsidiary within 30 days of approval with the adoption template.
Require each subsidiary board to adopt the policy by resolution or to adopt with documented local variations justified by national requirements.
Record adoption dates, local variations and their justification against the group policy record.
Escalate subsidiaries that have not adopted within one board cycle to the group Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: each group policy shows a subsidiary adoption resolution or a justified local variation for every entity in scope.

checklist.step: Report cycle status to the board and the Risk Committee
actions: Produce a quarterly status report: policies approved, in review, deferred and overdue, with days overdue and owner for each.
State explicitly whether every mandatory Art. 41(3) policy was covered by a valid board approval throughout the quarter.
Report open significant-change triggers and any policy the implementation check found unoperated.
Record the board's response and any instruction in the minute.
checklist.done: a quarterly status report with an explicit coverage statement and overdue ageing is minuted by the board.

checklist.step: Close overdue policies and record the gap
actions: For each policy past its anniversary, raise a governance exception recording the days overdue and whether the prior version remained in force and operated.
Assign the owner and a specific board meeting at which approval will be taken.
Assess and record whether the gap created any regulatory exposure and whether the NCA needs to be told.
Report residual overdue policies to the Audit Committee with the reason each remains open.
checklist.done: every overdue policy has an exception with days overdue, a named closure meeting and a recorded exposure assessment.

checklist.step: Retain the policy governance evidence
actions: File per policy and cycle: the approved version, the redline, the change brief, challenge comments, implementation status, board minute extract and communication records.
Apply the 10-year-from-supersession retention label and keep the full version chain so the policy in force on any past date can be reproduced.
Confirm the index makes versions searchable by policy name, entity, approval date and minute reference.
Grant Internal Audit and the external auditor read access to the current and prior two cycles.
checklist.done: the version chain and cycle evidence are retained for 10 years and the policy in force on any past date can be reproduced.

testing.step: Rebuild the population of policies in force during the period
actions: Extract the policy inventory with owner, entity scope, approving body, last approval date and next due date for every policy in force at any point in the period.
Independently derive the mandatory list from Art. 41(3) and Delegated Regulation Art. 258(1)(c) and compare it to the inventory to find missing policies.
Add the published policy library contents so policies in force but off the inventory are captured.
Sign the population as complete, recording the extraction date and sources.
testing.done: a signed population reconciles the inventory, the published library and the independently derived mandatory list.

testing.step: Reconcile approval dates to the board minutes
actions: For every policy in the population, locate the minute recording its approval and read the resolution wording.
Confirm the minute names the policy and the version that is actually published, not a generic 'policy pack' approval.
Compare the minute date to the approval date recorded in the GRC platform and log any difference.
List any policy whose recorded approval has no corresponding minute as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every recorded approval date is vouched to a minute naming the policy and version, with differences logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample for content and implementation testing
actions: Take 100% of the four Art. 41(3) mandatory policies and 100% of policies approved late or deferred in the period.
Take a seeded random selection of 10 further policies across entities and risk areas, minimum 20 policies overall.
Take 100% of policies named in an out-of-cycle significant-change review.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers the mandatory policies, all late or deferred approvals and all significant-change reviews.

testing.step: Re-perform the content standard assessment
actions: Score each sampled policy against the content standard yourself — regulatory basis and citations, scope, named responsibilities, limits, controls, reporting and escalation, breach handling, review frequency and approver.
Check the citations quoted are to the current text and that national requirements exceeding the Directive are reflected.
Compare your result to the recorded content-standard check and treat a passed check on a policy missing named responsibilities as a control failure.
Record the quoted clause relied on for each element scored as present.
testing.done: each sampled policy has an independent content score with a quoted clause for every element scored present.

testing.step: Test that the approved policy was actually operated
actions: Pick three testable requirements from each sampled policy — a report to be produced, a limit to be monitored, an approval to be taken.
Pull the operating evidence for each over the period and confirm frequency, ownership and escalation matched the policy text.
Where a requirement was not operated, check whether the board was told before it re-approved the policy.
Log re-approval of an unimplemented policy as a governance failure distinct from the operational gap itself.
testing.done: three requirements per sampled policy are tested against operating evidence and any re-approval of an unoperated policy is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the annual review deadline for every policy
actions: Recompute each policy's due date as the previous board approval date plus 12 months, taking the date from the minute rather than the GRC field.
Measure days overdue for every policy that missed its date and identify whether the undertaking operated without a valid approval in that window.
Confirm that where a policy was deferred, the prior approved version remained in force and was within its own validity.
Treat any mandatory policy overdue at period end as a fail regardless of the days count.
testing.done: every policy's 12-month deadline is recomputed from the minute date with days overdue measured and coverage gaps identified.

testing.step: Trace significant-change triggers to a review inside 3 months
actions: Independently build the list of significant changes in the period from board minutes, model change logs, the outsourcing register, incident records and acquisition approvals.
Compare it to the logged trigger list and treat any change absent from the log as an exception on sight.
For each change, recompute the 3-month review deadline and confirm the affected policies were reviewed and board-routed inside it.
Capture the change date, affected policies and review date into the workpaper.
testing.done: every independently identified significant change is matched to a logged trigger and a board-routed review inside 3 months.

testing.step: Test group cascade and subsidiary adoption
actions: For each sampled group policy, list the subsidiaries in scope and locate each one's adoption resolution or documented local variation.
Confirm adoption occurred within one board cycle of group approval and that variations are justified by a named national requirement.
Confirm the version adopted locally is the version the group board approved.
Flag subsidiaries operating on a superseded group version as an exception.
testing.done: every in-scope subsidiary shows a dated adoption of the correct version, or a justified variation, for each sampled group policy.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with policy name, entity, the requirement missed, days overdue where relevant and the governance consequence.
Assign a root cause (owner vacancy, cycle capacity, trigger not logged, approval taken below board, inventory drift) and an owner at function-head level.
Set a closure date tied to a named board meeting and require the approval minute as the closure artefact.
Escalate any mandatory Art. 41(3) policy without valid approval to the Board Chair and Chief Risk Officer within one business day.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, function-head owner, named closure meeting and required minute evidence.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the proportion of mandatory policies with valid board approval throughout the period and the on-time review rate.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — on whether the written-policy requirement of Art. 41(3) was met continuously.
Have an Internal Auditor who owns, drafted or approved no policy in the population sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Risk Committee and the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states a conclusion with coverage and on-time rates and a dated committee reporting entry.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the sustainability content of the ORSA — materiality assessment, climate scenario design and results — and the completion of EIOPA and NCA climate surveys; escalates to the Chief Risk Officer where a scenario result challenges the solvency needs assessment

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 262(1)(a) as amended by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2021/1256 (sustainability risks and climate-change scenarios in the assessment of overall solvency needs), read with Art. 269 and 275a on sustainability risks in risk management and remuneration, and the current Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/2450 Annex II instructions for templates S.02.01 and S.05.01, re-read at the start of each ORSA cycle

In-scope processes.value: Annual ORSA sustainability workstream: sustainability risk identification and materiality assessment across underwriting, investments, operations and reputational exposure → climate scenario specification → quantification of short, medium and long-term impacts → integration into the overall solvency needs assessment → board approval → ORSA supervisory report submission, plus completion of EIOPA and NCA climate and ESG surveys

In-scope systems.value: Sustainability risk register, materiality assessment and scenario results held in the GRC platform, with underwriting exposure from the catastrophe model, asset-side data from the investment platform, and the ORSA report and QRTs submitted through the NCA portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: Sustainability Risk and Climate Scenario Procedure for the ORSA — materiality methodology and thresholds, mandatory scenario set with transition and physical pathways, data sourcing, quantification approach, board reporting and the survey response process

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Risk Committee and adopted by the Board as part of the ORSA policy; reviewed annually and on any EIOPA opinion, NCA expectation or scenario-guidance update

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: ORSA supervisory report submitted to the NCA within 2 weeks of the assessment being concluded, per Delegated Regulation Art. 312(1); the sustainability workstream must close 6 weeks before the board ORSA approval date; EIOPA and NCA climate surveys are due on the date stated in the request letter, commonly 6 to 8 weeks from issue; S.02.01 and S.05.01 follow the annual QRT deadline of 14 weeks after year end for solo entities

Deadline reminders configured.value: The ORSA project plan raises tasks at T-16 weeks (materiality refresh), T-12 weeks (scenario specification signed off), T-8 weeks (quantification complete) and T-6 weeks (results to Risk Committee) against the board approval date, with survey requests logged on receipt and reminders at the response date minus 10 and minus 3 working days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Materiality assessment, scenario specification and calibration sources, model runs and results, board papers and minutes, the submitted ORSA report and every survey response with its supporting workings retained 10 years from submission

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Omitted material sustainability risks, scenarios not run, late survey responses and any inconsistency between the ORSA narrative and the submitted QRTs are logged with root cause and the ORSA cycle by which they must be resolved

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every conclusion that a sustainability risk is immaterial and every remediation of an ORSA or survey deficiency raised by the NCA

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The sustainability risk register and materiality assessment, every climate scenario specified and run for the ORSA cycle, the ORSA report sections covering sustainability, and every EIOPA or NCA climate and ESG survey response submitted in the period, across all solo entities and the group

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any sustainability risk assessed material but not quantified in a scenario is a fail; any scenario result that changes overall solvency needs by more than 5 percentage points of the solvency ratio and is not reflected in the ORSA conclusion is a fail; any survey submitted after its stated date without a written extension is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual through the ORSA cycle with event-driven surveys; the test runs once per ORSA cycle after board approval, plus a check on every survey response as it is submitted

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have specified, calibrated or run any scenario in the population, and must be outside the sustainability team

Evidence location for test results.value: ORSA sustainability test workpaper (materiality trace, scenario re-performance, data lineage, survey timeliness log, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository under ORSA and Sustainability

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Materiality assessment with thresholds, scenario specification and calibration sources, quantified results by risk and time horizon, and the board minute approving the conclusions, producible to the NCA or EIOPA within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Chief Risk Officer owns NCA engagement on ORSA sustainability findings; the Regulatory Reporting Manager submits survey responses and corrections, and the Board Chair is briefed before any commitment to change the risk appetite is given

checklist.step: Refresh the sustainability risk taxonomy and register
actions: Update the taxonomy to cover physical risk (acute and chronic), transition risk (policy, technology, market, reputation) and litigation risk, split by underwriting, investments, operations and third parties.
Map each taxonomy entry to the SII risk modules it touches — non-life catastrophe, market, counterparty default, operational — so the ORSA can connect it to the SCR.
Add each risk to the register with a named owner in the first line, the exposure metric that will measure it and the data source for that metric.
Circulate the refreshed register to the Chief Underwriting Officer, Chief Investment Officer and Chief Operating Officer for confirmation of ownership.
checklist.done: the register carries every taxonomy entry with an owner, an exposure metric, a data source and a mapping to the SII risk modules.

checklist.step: Assemble the underwriting exposure data for climate risk
actions: Extract the in-force property and casualty exposure by peril, geocoded location, construction, occupancy and sum insured as at the ORSA reference date.
Run the baseline catastrophe view for flood, windstorm, wildfire and subsidence and record the average annual loss and the 1-in-100 and 1-in-200 return period losses gross and net of reinsurance.
Score the geocoding quality and report the proportion of exposure resolved to street level rather than postcode centroid, since coarse geocoding understates flood results.
Hand the baseline and its data quality statement to the Sustainability Risk Manager.
checklist.done: a baseline catastrophe view exists by peril with gross and net return-period losses and a stated geocoding quality proportion.

checklist.step: Assemble the asset-side transition and physical exposure
actions: Extract the investment portfolio by asset class, issuer, sector and geography as at the reference date, with market values reconciled to the SII balance sheet.
Classify holdings by climate-relevant sector using the NACE codes and identify exposure to fossil fuel extraction, power generation, transport, real estate and heavy industry.
Obtain issuer-level carbon intensity and transition-plan data from the market data provider and record coverage — the proportion of the portfolio with actual rather than estimated data.
Reconcile the classified portfolio total to the S.02.01 asset lines so the ORSA and the QRT describe the same balance sheet.
checklist.done: the portfolio is classified by climate-relevant sector with stated data coverage and reconciled to the S.02.01 asset totals.

checklist.step: Run the materiality assessment against documented thresholds
actions: Score each register entry for likelihood and impact over short (1 year), medium (3 to 5 years) and long (10 years plus) horizons using the ORSA materiality thresholds.
Express impact in the same units as the solvency needs assessment — effect on own funds and on the solvency ratio — not in a colour rating alone.
For every risk concluded immaterial, record the quantitative basis and the Chief Risk Officer's sign-off; a narrative assertion is not sufficient.
Publish the material risk list as the input to scenario design and circulate it to the Risk Committee.
checklist.done: every register entry has a scored, threshold-based materiality conclusion in own-funds terms, with immateriality signed off by the CRO.

checklist.step: Specify the climate scenario set
actions: Specify at least one transition scenario consistent with an orderly path to net zero, one disorderly transition with delayed policy action, and one hot-house physical scenario with no further mitigation.

Set each scenario's calibration anchors — carbon price path, temperature pathway, hazard frequency and severity uplifts, sector repricing assumptions — and cite the published source for each, such as an NGFS pathway or an EIOPA reference scenario.
Define the time horizons and state how the scenario interacts with the business plan: run-off of current business versus assumed rewriting.
Take Risk Committee approval of the specification before quantification starts so results cannot be reverse-engineered to a preferred conclusion.
checklist.done: the scenario set is specified with cited calibration sources and horizons and is approved by the Risk Committee before quantification.

checklist.step: Quantify the underwriting impact of each scenario
actions: Apply each scenario's hazard uplift to the baseline catastrophe view and re-run the loss distribution for every peril and territory.
Recompute average annual loss and the 1-in-100 and 1-in-200 losses gross and net, and show the change against baseline in absolute and percentage terms.
Test reinsurance adequacy under the stressed view — whether the programme exhausts, and what the retained loss becomes.
Document the model version, event set, vulnerability curves and any judgemental adjustment applied, with the reason for each adjustment.
checklist.done: each scenario has stressed catastrophe results gross and net, a reinsurance exhaustion test and a documented model configuration.

checklist.step: Quantify the investment and counterparty impact
actions: Apply the scenario's sector repricing and credit migration assumptions to the classified portfolio and revalue holdings by asset class.
Compute the effect on the SII market risk and counterparty default modules and on the excess of assets over liabilities.
Test the liquidity consequence — whether a stressed sale would be needed to meet claims under the physical scenario in the same year.
Reconcile the stressed asset values to the same base as S.02.01 so the impact can be read against reported own funds.
checklist.done: each scenario has a revalued portfolio with market and counterparty module impacts and a liquidity test, reconciled to the S.02.01 base.

checklist.step: Assess operational, reputational and litigation exposure
actions: Assess physical risk to the firm's own premises, data centres and critical third parties using their site locations and the same hazard views.
Assess transition-related conduct and litigation exposure — greenwashing in product marketing, mis-stated sustainability claims, and third-party liability underwritten for high-emitting insureds.
Quantify the plausible loss for each and record it in the same own-funds terms as the other scenario results.
Coordinate with the Operational Resilience Lead so climate-driven disruption scenarios are consistent with the resilience testing programme.
checklist.done: operational, reputational and litigation exposures are quantified in own-funds terms and aligned with the resilience testing scenarios.

checklist.step: Integrate the results into the overall solvency needs assessment
actions: Aggregate the underwriting, investment, counterparty and operational impacts per scenario and per time horizon, stating the diversification treatment applied.
Compare the aggregated impact to the regulatory SCR and explain where the standard formula does not capture the risk, as Art. 262 requires the assessment to go beyond it.
Restate the projected solvency ratio under each scenario across the business planning horizon and identify the point at which any management action or capital action would be needed.
Show the effect on the risk appetite statement and name any limit that would be breached.
checklist.done: the ORSA states overall solvency needs under each scenario and horizon, with the gap to the standard formula and any limit breaches named.

checklist.step: Take the actuarial function's view on sustainability in underwriting and reserving
actions: Consider the scenario results when forming the Art. 48(1)(g) opinion on the overall underwriting policy, and state whether pricing and risk selection reflect the changing hazard.
Consider whether the reinsurance programme remains adequate under the stressed views for the Art. 48(1)(h) opinion.
State whether sustainability risks affect the assumptions underlying technical provisions, particularly for long-tail casualty and multi-year property exposure.
Deliver the written opinion into the ORSA pack with the date and the evidence relied on.
checklist.done: a dated actuarial opinion covering underwriting policy, reinsurance adequacy and technical provision assumptions is in the ORSA pack.

checklist.step: Take the results through the Risk Committee and the board
actions: Present the materiality assessment, scenario specification, quantified results and the actuarial opinion to the Risk Committee at T-6 weeks.
Record the committee's challenge on scenario severity, data coverage and management actions, and the resulting changes.
Take the board's approval of the ORSA including the sustainability conclusions, with the resolution wording and any conditions minuted.
Where the board disagrees with a conclusion, record the disagreement and the basis rather than reconciling it silently.
checklist.done: the sustainability conclusions carry minuted committee challenge and a board approval resolution with any disagreement recorded.

checklist.step: Submit the ORSA supervisory report and align the QRT narrative
actions: Submit the ORSA supervisory report to the NCA within 2 weeks of the assessment being concluded, per Delegated Regulation Art. 312(1), and record the submission reference and timestamp.
Check the sustainability narrative is consistent with the reported figures in S.02.01 (balance sheet) and S.05.01 (premiums, claims and expenses by line of business) for the same reference date.
Confirm the SFCR narrative on risk profile does not contradict the ORSA scenario conclusions.
File the submission receipt against the ORSA cycle record.
checklist.done: the ORSA report is submitted within 2 weeks of conclusion and its sustainability narrative reconciles to S.02.01 and S.05.01.

checklist.step: Respond to EIOPA and NCA climate and ESG surveys
actions: Log each survey request on receipt with the issuing authority, reference date, response deadline and the data template required.
Map every question to an existing ORSA, QRT or register source before answering, and answer from that source rather than compiling a fresh number.
Where the survey asks for data the firm does not hold, state that explicitly with the reason rather than estimating silently; where an estimate is used, label it and give the method.
Have the Chief Risk Officer review the response, then submit through the NCA channel and record the submission reference.
checklist.done: each survey response is sourced from ORSA or QRT records, labelled where estimated, CRO-reviewed and submitted with a recorded reference.

checklist.step: Convert the conclusions into tracked management actions
actions: Open an action for each management response the ORSA relied on — underwriting appetite change, reinsurance purchase, portfolio reallocation, data improvement.
Name the owner, the date and the evidence that will show it landed, and link the action to the scenario that motivated it.
Report progress quarterly to the Risk Committee so the next cycle can state whether prior actions were delivered.
Escalate any action that slips past the next ORSA cycle since the solvency needs assessment relied on it.
checklist.done: every management action relied on in the ORSA has an owner, a date, linked evidence and quarterly committee reporting.

checklist.step: Retain the sustainability evidence pack
actions: File the materiality assessment, scenario specification with calibration sources, model run logs and results, board papers and minutes, the submitted ORSA report and every survey response with its workings.
Apply the 10-year-from-submission retention label and record the model and data versions so a result can be reproduced years later.
Confirm the index makes the pack searchable by ORSA cycle, entity, scenario name and survey reference.
Grant Internal Audit and the Model Risk Manager read access for the independent review.
checklist.done: the pack is filed with model and data versions recorded, labelled for 10-year retention and searchable by cycle and scenario.

testing.step: Build the population of sustainability risks, scenarios and survey responses
actions: Extract the sustainability risk register with materiality scores, owners and exposure metrics as at the ORSA reference date.
List every scenario specified for the cycle with its calibration sources and every model run executed against it.
List every EIOPA and NCA climate or ESG survey received in the period from the regulatory correspondence register, including any not answered.
Sign the population as complete, recording the extraction date and the sources reconciled.
testing.done: a signed population covers every registered risk, specified scenario, executed run and received survey, including unanswered ones.

testing.step: Reconcile the exposure inputs to the source of record
actions: Agree the in-force exposure used in the catastrophe baseline to the policy administration in-force extract for the reference date by peril and territory.
Agree the investment portfolio market values used in the transition analysis to the S.02.01 asset lines and the custodian statement.
Confirm the geocoding quality and issuer data coverage percentages quoted in the ORSA match the underlying files.
List any input that cannot be reconciled as an automatic exception before any results are tested.
testing.done: underwriting and investment inputs reconcile to the policy admin extract, S.02.01 and the custodian record, with quoted coverage verified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of risks assessed material and 100% of risks assessed immaterial where the exposure metric exceeds the materiality threshold.
Take 100% of scenarios and a seeded random selection of 15 model runs across perils, territories and asset classes.
Take 100% of survey responses submitted in the period.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all material risks, contradictory immateriality calls, all scenarios and all survey responses.

testing.step: Re-perform the materiality assessment on the sample
actions: Apply the documented thresholds to the sampled risks' exposure metrics yourself before reading the recorded conclusion.
Confirm impact was expressed in own-funds or solvency-ratio terms rather than a colour rating alone.
For every immateriality conclusion, confirm a quantitative basis and a dated Chief Risk Officer sign-off exist.
Log any risk assessed material but absent from the scenario quantification as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled materiality conclusion is independently re-derived and every material risk is confirmed present in a scenario.

testing.step: Re-perform selected scenario results in the modelling systems
actions: Re-run the sampled catastrophe runs using the recorded model version, event set and hazard uplift and compare the average annual loss and 1-in-200 result to the reported figures.
Re-apply the sector repricing and credit migration assumptions to the classified portfolio and compare the revalued own funds to the reported impact.
Confirm every judgemental adjustment is documented with a reason and was applied before, not after, the result was seen.
Treat a right answer produced from an undocumented configuration as an exception.
testing.done: sampled scenario results are independently re-run from the recorded configuration and differences from the reported figures are logged.

testing.step: Verify calibration sources against the cited publications
actions: For each scenario, open the cited source — the NGFS pathway, EIOPA reference scenario or hazard study — and confirm the carbon price path, temperature pathway and hazard uplifts match what was applied.
Confirm the version and publication date of the source and that it was current at the specification date.
Check the specification was approved by the Risk Committee before the runs were executed, using the minute date and the run timestamps.
Flag any calibration that cannot be traced to a published source or an approved internal expert judgement paper.
testing.done: every calibration anchor traces to a dated published source and the specification approval pre-dates the model runs.

testing.step: Trace ORSA conclusions to the quantified results and the QRTs
actions: Take each sustainability conclusion in the submitted ORSA report and locate the quantified result and the workpaper cell it came from.
Confirm the balance sheet and premium figures quoted in the narrative agree to the submitted S.02.01 and S.05.01 for the same reference date.
Confirm the SFCR risk profile narrative and the ORSA do not describe the exposure differently.
Log any conclusion supported only by narrative as an unsupported assertion.
testing.done: each ORSA sustainability conclusion traces to a quantified result and reconciles to the submitted S.02.01 and S.05.01.

testing.step: Recompute submission and survey timeliness
actions: Identify the date the assessment was concluded from the board minute and recompute the ORSA submission due date as that date plus 2 weeks under Art. 312(1).
Compare the NCA acknowledgement timestamp to the recomputed date and log any late submission.
For each survey, recompute the response deadline from the request letter and compare it to the submission timestamp, checking any extension is evidenced in writing.
Confirm the annual S.02.01 and S.05.01 were filed within 14 weeks of the financial year end.
testing.done: ORSA, survey and QRT submissions are each proven against a recomputed statutory or stated deadline.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the risk or scenario name, entity, what failed and the effect on the reported solvency needs assessment.
Assign a root cause (risk not registered, data coverage gap, scenario not run, calibration unsourced, survey deadline missed, narrative not reconciled) and an owner.
Set a remediation date inside the next ORSA cycle and require the corrected run or resubmission as the closure artefact.
Escalate anything that materially changed the reported solvency ratio to the Chief Risk Officer and the Board Chair within one business day.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, an in-cycle remediation date and a named closure artefact.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
