actions: Compute the proportion of material sustainability risks quantified in a scenario and the on-time rate for ORSA and survey submissions.

State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — on whether sustainability risks including climate-change scenarios were properly considered in the overall solvency needs assessment.
Have the Model Risk Manager, who specified, calibrated and ran none of the scenarios, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Risk Committee and the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states a conclusion with quantification coverage and on-time rates and a dated committee reporting entry.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the internal model data directory and the accuracy, completeness and appropriateness standards behind it, reporting to the Chief Risk Officer as the risk management function accountable for internal model data quality

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Solvency II Directive 2009/138/EC Art. 121(3) (data used in the internal model must be accurate, complete and appropriate) and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 244 (data quality standards and the directory of data specifying source, characteristics and usage), read with Art. 260(1)(a) on the risk management function's tasks, re-checked at each annual data policy review and on any model change application

In-scope processes.value: Internal model data lifecycle: source system identification → ingestion and transformation into the model data mart → data directory maintenance → data quality measurement against accuracy, completeness and appropriateness → limitation and adjustment recording → validation and model change control, covering every data item feeding the internal model and the methodology workpapers supporting it

In-scope systems.value: Data directory and quality rule results held in the data catalog, lineage and transformations in the pipeline orchestrator and warehouse, model configurations and methodology papers in the model governance repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Internal Model Data Policy and Directory Procedure — directory content standard (source, characteristics, usage), data quality dimensions and measurement rules, materiality-based thresholds, limitation and expert-judgement recording, update triggers and the annual attestation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board as part of the data quality policy required by Delegated Regulation Art. 258(1)(c), recommended by the Risk Committee; reviewed annually and before any major model change application to the NCA

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous obligation with fixed anchors — directory entries updated within 20 working days of any source, transformation or usage change; data quality measurement run every calculation cycle before the SCR is signed; the annual data quality report to the Risk Committee before the model validation report is finalised; the directory must be current at the date of any model change application to the NCA

Deadline reminders configured.value: The data catalog raises a task on every schema or lineage change affecting a directory entry with a 20-working-day clock, an annual review task per data steward 90 days before the attestation date, and a blocking task in the calculation cycle if any critical rule is unrun

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Directory versions, data quality rule definitions and results per cycle, limitation and expert-judgement records, remediation evidence and the annual attestation retained 10 years from the date the model version is retired

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Undirectoried data items used in a calculation, critical rules breached, unrecorded expert judgement and stale directory entries are logged as internal model data deficiencies with materiality, owner and remediation cycle

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every data deficiency and confirms whether the deficiency requires disclosure in the model validation report or notification to the NCA

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every data item used by the internal model in the calculation cycles under test — directory entries, source systems, transformation steps, quality rule results, recorded limitations and expert judgements — across all entities within the internal model scope

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on directory completeness — any data item used in a calculation with no directory entry is a fail; critical-rule pass rate must be 100% and non-critical at least 98%; any expert judgement applied without a dated, approved record is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the test runs quarterly against that quarter's calculation cycle, with a full annual re-performance of directory completeness and lineage ahead of the model validation report

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the model development and data engineering teams and must not own any directory entry or quality rule in the population

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly internal model data quality test workpaper (directory completeness reconciliation, lineage trace, rule re-performance, limitation review, exception list) in the model governance repository under the model version and cycle

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The data directory export with source, characteristics and usage per item, the data quality results for the cycle, the limitation register and the annual attestation, producible to the NCA within 5 business days of an internal model review or model change assessment

Regulator response path.value: Model Risk Manager owns NCA questions on internal model data quality with the Chief Risk Officer accountable; General Counsel clears any response conceding that unvalidated data entered an approved model calculation

checklist.step: Define the internal model data scope
actions: List every calculation component of the internal model — exposure, claims history, policy terms, reinsurance structures, asset holdings, economic scenario inputs, expenses, dependency parameters — and the data items each consumes.
Distinguish data used directly in the calculation from data used to set assumptions and from data used only for reporting, since Art. 244 applies differently to each.
Confirm the scope against the model documentation and the NCA's model approval decision so nothing in the approved scope is left out.
Publish the scope list as the control list against which directory completeness is measured.
checklist.done: a published scope list names every data item consumed by each model component, split by direct calculation, assumption setting and reporting use.

checklist.step: Create or refresh the directory entry for each data item
actions: For every item on the scope list, create a catalog entry recording the source — system of record, table and field, extraction method and frequency — as Art. 244 requires.
Record the characteristics: business definition, data type, unit of measure, currency, permitted values or code set, granularity, effective-dating rule and known limitations.
Record the usage: which model component consumes it, in which calculation step, and whether it drives a result directly or an assumption.
Name the accountable data steward and the technical owner and set the review cycle.
checklist.done: every scope item has a catalog entry with source, characteristics, usage, a named steward and a review cycle.

checklist.step: Capture end-to-end lineage from source to model input
actions: Map each directory entry to its pipeline: extraction job, staging table, transformation steps with their business rules, and the model input table and column.
Record every transformation that changes meaning — currency conversion, aggregation, netting of reinsurance, exclusion filters, default value substitution — with the rule and its owner.
Publish the lineage graph in the catalog and confirm it is generated from the pipeline metadata rather than hand-drawn.
Flag any model input with no traced lineage as an immediate blocking issue for the next calculation cycle.
checklist.done: each directory entry has machine-generated lineage to its model input column with every meaning-changing transformation recorded.

checklist.step: Set the data quality rules against the three regulatory dimensions
actions: For accuracy, define value-range, referential-integrity, reconciliation-to-source and cross-field consistency rules per item.
For completeness, define population coverage rules — expected record counts, mandatory field fill rates, and history depth sufficient for the statistical method used.
For appropriateness, define rules on granularity, relevance to the risk being modelled, homogeneity of the grouping and absence of structural change in the historical period.
Classify each rule critical or non-critical, set its threshold, and record who approved the threshold and on what basis.
checklist.done: each directory entry has approved accuracy, completeness and appropriateness rules with thresholds and a critical or non-critical classification.

checklist.step: Run the rules as a gate in every calculation cycle
actions: Schedule the rule pack to run against the frozen model input set before the SCR calculation starts, not after results are produced.
Publish the cycle scorecard by model component with rule pass rates, records failed and the direction of any trend against prior cycles.
Block the calculation where any critical rule fails and require an approved override with a named approver and a stated reason to proceed.
Record the rule pack version and run identifiers on the cycle record so the gate can be re-performed later.
checklist.done: the rule pack runs before each calculation with a published scorecard, and critical failures block the run unless an approved override is recorded.

checklist.step: Reconcile model inputs back to the systems of record
actions: For each material data item, reconcile control totals — record counts, sums of exposure, premium, reserves and asset market values — between the source system, the warehouse and the model input table.
Explain every difference by a documented transformation rule rather than accepting it as timing.
Agree the asset-side totals to the SII balance sheet and the liability-side totals to the technical provisions used in the same cycle.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the cycle record.
checklist.done: control totals reconcile source to warehouse to model input for every material item, with each difference explained by a named rule.

checklist.step: Record limitations, deficiencies and their materiality
actions: Maintain a limitation register listing each known data deficiency — short history, coarse granularity, missing exposure attributes, proxy data used for a subsidiary — with the model component affected.
Assess and record the materiality of each limitation on the SCR result, quantitatively where possible, and the direction of the bias it introduces.
Record the compensating action: adjustment applied, additional margin, restricted use of the affected component, or acceptance with monitoring.
Report the register to the Risk Committee each cycle and flag any limitation that has grown in materiality.
checklist.done: every known limitation is registered with its model impact, direction of bias, compensating action and a committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Document expert judgement and data adjustments
actions: Record each expert judgement applied to data — outlier removal, event exclusion, on-levelling, trend adjustment, proxy substitution — with the rationale, the alternatives considered and the quantified effect on the result.
Name the person who made the judgement, the person who approved it and the date, and cross-reference it to the directory entry it modifies.
State how the judgement will be revisited and what evidence would overturn it.
Refuse to carry forward a judgement into a new cycle without an explicit re-confirmation.
checklist.done: each expert judgement has a rationale, quantified effect, maker and approver names, a date and a re-confirmation requirement.

checklist.step: Remediate failures at source rather than in the model
actions: Route each rule failure to the accountable source-system owner — underwriting, claims, investment operations or reinsurance — with the failing records attached.
Set the remediation route: correct at source, change the source system control, or amend the transformation where the rule was wrong.
Set a target cycle for closure and require evidence of the rule passing in a later run before the issue is closed.
Escalate items open for more than two calculation cycles to the Chief Data Officer and the Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: every rule failure has a source-side owner, a remediation route, a target cycle and closure evidenced by a subsequent passing run.

checklist.step: Keep the directory current when anything changes
actions: Subscribe the catalog to schema-change and pipeline-change events so any change to a source field or transformation raises a directory review task.
Update the affected entry within 20 working days of the change taking effect, recording the old and new values and the change reference.
Where a new data item enters the model, complete its directory entry, rules and lineage before it is used in a calculation, not after.
Report stale entries — those past their review cycle — on the monthly data governance dashboard.
checklist.done: directory entries are updated within 20 working days of any change and no new data item is used before its entry, rules and lineage exist.

checklist.step: Maintain the methodology workpapers behind the model
actions: Keep a methodology paper per model component stating the statistical method, the data period used, the fitting and parameterisation approach, goodness-of-fit evidence and the rejected alternatives.
Cross-reference every data item the method relies on to its directory entry so the reader can move from method to source without asking.
Version the paper alongside the model version and record which paper version supported which calculation cycle.
Archive superseded versions rather than overwriting so a past result remains explainable.
checklist.done: each model component has a versioned methodology paper cross-referenced to directory entries and tied to the cycles it supported.

checklist.step: Feed data quality into model validation
actions: Supply the validation team with the directory export, cycle scorecards, the limitation register and the expert judgement log for the validation period.
Require validation to test data quality independently and to state a conclusion on accuracy, completeness and appropriateness in the validation report.
Track every validation finding on data to closure with an owner and a cycle, and report open findings to the Risk Committee.
Ensure no model change application goes to the NCA while a material data finding is open without disclosing it.
checklist.done: the validation report carries an independent conclusion on the three data dimensions and every data finding is tracked with an owner and cycle.

checklist.step: Control data changes inside the model change policy
actions: Classify each data-related change as major or minor under the model change policy using its quantified SCR impact.
Route minor changes through the internal model change committee and log them in the change register for periodic NCA reporting.
Route major changes to the NCA for approval before use and do not run the affected component on the changed basis until approval is received.
Record the approval reference and effective date against the directory entries the change touched.
checklist.done: every data-related change is classified, routed and logged, with major changes unused until an NCA approval reference is recorded.

checklist.step: Attest annually to directory completeness and data quality
actions: Require each data steward to attest that their directory entries are complete and current and that the rules in place are sufficient for the usage recorded.
Reconcile the scope list to the directory and confirm zero unmatched items before the attestation is signed.
Sign the consolidated annual data quality report covering accuracy, completeness and appropriateness by model component, with the open limitation register attached.
Present the report to the Risk Committee and the Board before the model validation report is finalised.
checklist.done: a signed annual attestation and data quality report with zero unmatched scope items is presented to the Risk Committee and Board.

checklist.step: Retain the directory and data quality evidence
actions: Archive per cycle: the directory export, rule definitions and results, reconciliations, limitation register, expert judgement log, override approvals and the attestation.
Apply the 10-year-from-model-retirement retention label and record the model version and rule pack version so the cycle can be reconstructed.
Confirm the index makes evidence searchable by model version, cycle, data item and steward.
Grant Internal Audit, model validation and the external auditor read access to the current and prior two years.
checklist.done: each cycle's data evidence is archived with model and rule pack versions, labelled for retention and searchable by data item and cycle.

testing.step: Build the population of data items used in the cycle
actions: Extract the model input tables and columns actually consumed by the calculation run for the cycle from the run configuration, not from the documentation.
Extract the directory as at the run date with source, characteristics, usage, steward and review date per entry.
Build the population as one row per consumed data item with its directory entry status.
Sign the population as complete, recording the run identifier, extraction date and queries used.
testing.done: a signed population lists every data item the calculation actually consumed, matched to its directory entry status.

testing.step: Reconcile directory completeness against consumption
actions: Match consumed items to directory entries and list items consumed with no entry, and entries with no consumption.
For each unmatched consumed item, identify the model component it fed and quantify its influence on the SCR result.
Compare the result to the scope list published by the Model Risk Manager and explain any difference between scope, directory and consumption.
Treat any item consumed without a directory entry as an automatic fail under Art. 244.
testing.done: consumption, directory and scope are reconciled three ways with every undirectoried consumed item quantified and failed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of data items feeding the three model components with the largest SCR contribution and 100% of items with an open limitation or expert judgement.
Take a seeded random selection of 20 further items spread across sources and model components, minimum 40 items overall.
Take 100% of critical-rule overrides approved during the cycle.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers the highest-contribution components, all limitations and judgements, and every critical-rule override.

testing.step: Re-perform the lineage trace on the sample
actions: For each sampled item, open the pipeline definition and walk source table and field, staging, transformations and model input column yourself.
Compare your trace to the published lineage and to the directory's stated source, flagging any undocumented transformation.
Pick one record per sampled item and follow its value end to end, confirming each transformation produced the value in the model input.
Log a right value produced by an undocumented rule as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled item has an independent lineage walk plus a single-record end-to-end value trace, with undocumented transformations logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the data quality rules and check the thresholds
actions: Re-run the accuracy, completeness and appropriateness rules for the sampled items against the frozen cycle input and compare to the published scorecard.
Confirm each rule's critical or non-critical classification and threshold were approved and unchanged during the cycle.
Test that rules actually run before the calculation started by comparing rule run timestamps to the calculation start timestamp.
Check the 100% critical and 98% non-critical thresholds were met, and where an override was used, that a named approver and stated reason exist.
testing.done: sampled rule results are independently re-run, thresholds verified as approved, and rule timing proven to precede the calculation.

testing.step: Reconcile model inputs to the systems of record
actions: Independently pull control totals from the source systems for the sampled items and compare them to the model input totals.
Agree asset totals to the SII balance sheet and liability totals to the technical provisions used in the same cycle.
Vouch every reconciling difference to a documented transformation rule, not to an explanatory narrative.
List unvouched differences as exceptions with their quantified effect.
testing.done: independently derived control totals agree to the model inputs and to the balance sheet, with each difference vouched to a rule.

testing.step: Test limitations and expert judgements for support and currency
actions: For each sampled limitation, confirm the materiality assessment is quantified, states the direction of bias and names a compensating action that was actually applied.
For each expert judgement, confirm the rationale, alternatives considered, quantified effect, maker, approver and date are all present.
Confirm judgements carried into the cycle were explicitly re-confirmed rather than inherited silently.
Recompute the quantified effect of two judgements and compare to the recorded figure.
testing.done: each sampled limitation and judgement is fully supported, re-confirmed for the cycle, and two effects are independently recomputed.

testing.step: Recompute directory currency and change-control timing
actions: List every schema, pipeline or usage change affecting a sampled item during the period from the change management records.
Recompute the directory update deadline as the change effective date plus 20 working days and measure the actual update date against it.
For each data-related model change, confirm the major or minor classification against its quantified SCR impact and, for major changes, that an NCA approval reference pre-dates first use.
Log any component run on a changed basis before approval as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: every change has a recomputed 20-day directory deadline and every major change is proven approved before first use.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation cycle
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the data item, model component, the requirement missed and the quantified effect on the SCR.
Assign a root cause (item never directoried, lineage undocumented, rule threshold unapproved, judgement unrecorded, change not propagated) and an owner in the source or data engineering function.
Set a remediation cycle and require a subsequent passing rule run or an updated directory entry as the closure artefact.
Escalate any undirectoried item that materially influenced the SCR to the Chief Risk Officer and Model Risk Manager within one business day.
testing.done: every exception has an issue with quantified SCR effect, root cause, owner, remediation cycle and a named closure artefact.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute directory completeness as consumed items with an entry over total consumed items, and the critical and non-critical rule pass rates for the cycle.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — on whether internal model data met the accurate, complete and appropriate standard of Art. 121(3) and Art. 244.
Have the Model Risk Manager, who owns no directory entry or rule in the population and sits outside model development, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Risk Committee and the Audit Committee, supply the conclusion to model validation, and file the signed workpaper in the model governance repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states a conclusion with directory completeness and rule pass rates and a dated committee reporting entry.
